## KI#189 - (Fixed/Improved) Major UWAI issue: repeated random reviews could cancel or redirect most war preparations before they became wars

BBAI diagnostics in save file 452 showed that the AI frequently began preparing a war, mobilized around that plan, and then discarded or redirected it before fighting. Across all civilization AIs, 152 preparations began, 130 were canceled or switched away from, and only 17 became wars. China was the clearest individual example: it began 36 preparations, had 19 canceled by the inherited random-abandonment roll, switched target 13 times, and turned only 2 preparations into wars. Repeated mobilization without commitment wastes military tempo and can keep units concentrated around plans that never produce a conquest or defensive result.

The main cause was not simply that war utility sometimes became negative. UWAI converted the negative utility, leader `WarRand`, and game speed into an abandonment probability and rolled it on every negative review. The save-file 452 baseline contained 120 such checks and 69 random cancellations. Repeated rolls make even a moderate chance cumulative: an unchanged 20% chance is about 67% over five reviews and about 89% over ten. A mildly doubtful plan was therefore likely to disappear eventually even when no decisive strategic deterioration occurred.

Two other inherited rolls made the result less stable. UWAI used the relative benefit of the best alternative target as a probability of switching rather than as a requirement, so a small improvement could sometimes redirect an established preparation while a large improvement could sometimes be ignored. It also randomly selected the utility threshold for changing from preparation to a direct war plan, making otherwise identical readiness decisions conclude on different turns. The baseline produced 22 target switches from 71 comparisons.

This instability could immediately contradict fresh scheming. Of the 74 baseline cancellations, 32 selected the same target again on the same team turn and 41 did so within three turns. The current-plan review and the fresh-plan evaluation legitimately use different preparation horizons, so a mature plan can sometimes be unattractive as an immediate war but attractive again with more preparation time. However, canceling and recreating it on the same turn is never useful, and newly selected plans also need a short commitment period so transient UWAI or AreaAI changes do not erase them after their first review.

AdvCiv-SAS now makes preparation review deterministic and gives commitment already spent on mobilization appropriate weight:

- the old personality- and game-speed-adjusted abandonment value is retained as a severity score rather than rerolled as a probability; the XML-tunable default requires the maximum 100% severity;
- severity alone cannot abandon a preparation before the XML-tunable age 3, giving it two full reviews to settle, while illegal targets, expired preparations with negative utility, and imminent-war failures remain immediate;
- the best alternative target must reach an XML-tunable 50% relative-advantage score to switch reliably; smaller fluctuations never switch, and qualifying alternatives no longer depend on another roll;
- imminent plans always perform that meaningful-advantage comparison instead of first rolling whether to look for a better target;
- the direct-war threshold uses the old random range's midpoint, preserving its preparation-time progression without making readiness depend on a dice roll;
- a target whose plan changed during review cannot be reconsidered by fresh scheming later in the same team turn, but all other targets remain available and the changed target can be reconsidered normally on a later turn.

The investigation also found an AdvCiv-SAS integration bug in victory denial. `doScheme` added urgency when selecting a rival close to victory, but later inherited war-plan review omitted the boost. In the save-file 452 baseline, China selected India on turn 237 at utility `320` (`20 + 300` victory denial), then reviewed the same preparation at only `17` on turn 238 and switched away. Similar attempts were canceled and immediately selected again. Reviews and alternative-target comparisons now retain the same victory-denial value. If an existing preparation later passes the narrow distance, power, naval, and countdown gates from KI#184, it can declare immediately instead of waiting for another scheming cycle.

The final save-file 452 confirming run reduced cancellations from 74 to 34 and target switches from 22 to 15 while increasing actual wars from 22 to 29. Same-turn reselection fell from 32 to 0, and reselection within three turns fell from 41 to 5. All deterministic decisions matched their XML thresholds: every severity cancellation scored 100, continued checks scored 2-98, accepted switches scored at least 51, and rejected switches scored at most 49. The age grace protected 15 preparation episodes; plans that remained decisively bad could still be canceled from age 3 onward, while others recovered, continued below the severity threshold, switched to a clearly better target, or advanced to direct war.

Save file 450 independently confirmed the behavior over 418 preparation reviews: 39 preparations advanced to direct war and 35 wars started. The run had no same-turn cancel/reselect case, no severity cancellation before age 3, 14 severity cancellations all at exactly 100, and 109 post-grace negative checks from 1-95 that correctly continued. All 21 target switches scored at least 51 while all 66 rejected comparisons scored at most 49. Three existing victory-denial preparations newly passed the direct-war gates during review; each declaration appeared in the game record, including wars against the eventual Space threats on turns 255 and 281.

The cure intentionally does not forbid every later return to a mature or expired target. In the save-file 450 confirmation, 15 of 38 cancellations prepared against the same target again within three turns, mainly after a full preparation deadline, an imminent-war timeout, or a mature severe deterioration. A longer preparation horizon can genuinely make such a war attractive again. The fixed issue is premature and roll-dependent loss of commitment, especially same-turn contradictions, not legitimate later reconsideration after the plan or strategic timing has changed.

Fixed/improved with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex) thanks.

<a id="ki-189.2"></a>

## KI#189.2 - (Fixed/Improved) Base AdvCiv UWAI issues: volatile war estimates, compounding random peace rolls and excessive future-war costs could prematurely end profitable campaigns

The broad short-war investigation found an ongoing-war counterpart to KI#189. Base AdvCiv UWAI could start peace negotiations whenever its current war value fell below the context-sensitive peace threshold. Instead of requiring a clearly bad result, it converted the size of the deficit into a random chance and rolled again on every review. Repeated chances accumulate: even an unchanged 10% chance produces about a 65% chance of at least one successful roll over ten reviews. This made a useful war increasingly likely to end merely because it continued long enough, and a temporary one-turn fluctuation could decide the outcome.

Conversely, a clearly harmful war could keep going when its roll failed. This randomness did not add useful strategic variety: the calculation had already compared continuing the war with peace, and the repeated roll could either discard a modest advantage or delay escaping a major loss. Human peace contact still benefits from personality-based timing, but AI-vs-AI peace can respond directly to the strategic result.

Save-file 452 showed how volatile the old decision input could be. Egypt had captured population-12 Satsuma from Japan, led by 8 cities to 5, 762 power to 550, war success 99 to 64 and field army 36 to 8, with 20 Egyptian units in Japan and a technological lead. Nevertheless, its peace value briefly fell to `-32`. A first deterministic prototype with only a 15-point tolerance immediately ended the advantageous war on turn 152. The estimate rebounded to `+87` only one turn later and then remained strongly positive, confirming that the negative review was a temporary dip rather than a durable reason to stop.

Mali provided a second independent example in the same prototype. Its India war changed from `+107` on turn 166 to `-19` on turn 167 even though Mali led by 6 cities to 5, 1146 power to 891, war success 42 to 0 and field army 28 to 6; it had 20 units in India, had won 12 logged battles without a loss and was attacking Delhi. The 15-point prototype again made immediate peace. These examples showed that removing the random roll alone was insufficient: the deterministic replacement also needed enough margin to ignore ordinary one-turn variation.

AI-vs-AI peace initiation now uses `SAS_UWAI_AI_PEACE_DECISIVE_UTILITY_MARGIN`, default 40. A deficit smaller than 40 is not enough for the AI to initiate peace, although its opponent can still offer a treaty or capitulation that the AI finds acceptable. Once the deficit reaches 40, the AI seeks peace immediately instead of rolling. Emergency multi-war peace remains immediate, and peace contact with a human retains its inherited personality-based pacing.

The same-history confirming run demonstrated both sides of the final rule. Egypt continued its Japan war through the `-32` review, rebounded to `+87` on the next turn and captured population-7 Tokyo on turn 165. Continuing was not free: from turns 152-175 Egypt recorded 30 kills and 43 losses. When Japan later requested peace at a much worse `-47`, Egypt accepted after gaining the additional city, so the margin preserved useful pressure without trapping the AI in the war after costly attrition. Mali likewise continued through a `-7` dip, then accepted India's request at `-70` one turn later.

The investigation also found a separate Base AdvCiv valuation problem that could overwhelm an otherwise successful war. UWAI's `Distraction` aspect treats other wars and war preparations as opportunity costs of continuing the current war. In the save-file 452 baseline, Mali had 7 cities against Maya's 3, 891 power against 397 and an 83-point war-success lead, and the current war still had positive value before `Distraction`. A new preparation against India nevertheless increased this cost from `-18` to `-96` and caused Mali to make peace with Maya. The AI could therefore abandon a weak opponent it was already defeating because it had begun considering a separate future war.

For a clearly winning current war, `Distraction` is now capped by two XML-tunable safeguards. The target must have no more than `SAS_UWAI_DISTRACTION_WINNING_WAR_MAX_TARGET_POWER_PERCENT` of the AI's power, default 50%; the AI must also have more cities, positive current-war value before `Distraction`, and a war-success lead worth at least one city capture. Only then is the total `Distraction` cost capped at `SAS_UWAI_DISTRACTION_WINNING_WAR_MAX_COST_PERCENT`, default 15% of that positive current-war value. Effort, risk, war weariness and the emergency danger from fighting several enemies remain valued separately, so the cap does not disguise an exhausted or strategically dangerous war.

A 50% cost-cap prototype kept Mali fighting long enough to capture another Maya city, but its turn-161 review still reached `-21` and continued only because a 14% peace roll happened to fail. The final 15% cap preserves a modest opportunity cost while preventing a newly considered war from erasing the value of decisively defeating the current opponent. History divergence meant that the exact Mali-Maya branch did not recur under the final value, but the prototype established the cause and benefit, and later diagnostics confirmed that qualifying `Distraction` costs were constrained as intended.

In the final full run, all 7 marginal AI-vs-AI reviews continued, 139 decisive reviews sought peace immediately, and no AI-vs-AI peace decision used the old random roll. Ordinary early wars still lasted 8, 24, 25 and 30 turns. A two-turn war that ended successfully was not a regression: its initiating AI was already at `-76` against an opponent with 157% of its power. The resulting decisions are more stable without making every war long or preventing rational early peace.

Fixed/improved with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex) thanks.

<a id="ki-190"></a>

## KI#190 - (Fixed/Improved) Base AdvCiv/K-Mod issue: anti-Space armies could attack other cities or spend the launch countdown on ordinary tactics instead of trying to capture the spaceship owner's capital

KI#184 and KI#184.2 made AIs start and preserve wars against serious victory threats, but the city-assault AI did not know the decisive objective after a spaceship launched. It still compared cities through ordinary conquest value, so an easy nearby capture could beat the current capital even though only the capital could stop the imminent Space victory. BBAI save-file 450 testing showed Pataliputra score `318888` against Delhi's `26333`, Djenne score `249333` against Delhi's `3477`, and Bombay score `798444` against Delhi's `64588`. Capturing those cities could weaken India, but it did not reset India's launch countdown.

Base AdvCiv added only 10 to the capital's raw target value at late Space stage. Distance, defenses and other tactical multipliers were applied afterward, so merely increasing that additive value could not reliably overcome differences such as `249333` against `3477` without also distorting ordinary conquest decisions. `SAS_AI_SPACE4_CAPITAL_TARGET_VALUE_BONUS`, default 10, now exposes the inherited preference for tuning, but it remains an ordinary city-value adjustment rather than the emergency cure.

The investigation also corrected the intended scope. `CvCity::kill` calls `CvTeam::resetVictoryProgress` when a capital is lost, but that function removes spaceship projects only for a victory whose countdown is already active. Before launch, spaceship components are team-wide projects rather than objects stored in the capital: capturing the capital merely relocates it and preserves the completed parts. One prototype empirically chased England through successive capitals while England retained 75% spaceship completion. A hard capital override would therefore be wasteful before launch; after launch, however, capturing or razing the current capital resets the active countdown and removes the completed spaceship projects, immediately preventing that Space victory.

With `SAS_AI_SPACE_VICTORY_DENIAL_CAPITAL_RUSH_ENABLE` enabled, a civilization AI city-assault group at war now separately ranks launched-spaceship capitals that it can reach within the remaining countdown. The shortest countdown has priority, followed by greater spaceship completion, a shorter route and then ordinary target value. This emergency selection cannot be defeated by the value of an easier non-capital city. Base AdvCiv's existing estimate of enough offense already traveling toward a target remains in effect, so every surplus army does not have to converge on the same capital. Once the capital falls and the countdown resets, ordinary city targeting resumes.

Selection alone was not enough. In an early save-file 450 test, Egypt selected launched Cahokia 33 times, but normal K-Mod execution still spent the countdown on opportunistic combat, grouping, healing retreats and other waits; the main army's remaining route changed from five turns to two and then back to four and three before Native America won. The cure therefore lets a reachable launched-capital objective move directly before those generic alternatives, while preserving the normal adjacent bombard and attack decisions. When an army's immediate strength is below the normal attack threshold after those checks, it waits once it is within one path turn so it can recover or receive reinforcements without advancing beside the city too early. If no countdown slack remains, it attempts the capital assault even at unfavorable odds because preserving the army while certainly losing the game is no longer useful.

Focused testing found and fixed one last mismatch between those stages. A roughly 50-unit Native American army reached Delhi's attack tile but failed to act for five turns: K-Mod's projected post-bombard comparison considered it ready, its immediate attack comparison declined the assault, and its movement helper correctly returned false because it was already on the preferred adjacent plot. A later London run measured the same disagreement precisely: immediate strength `108` was below the required `121`, while projected post-bombard strength was `130` even though that group could not bombard. The emergency hold now uses immediate strength, while the projected value remains available for normal bombard planning. The next confirming run recorded 49 direct advances, 16 deliberate understrength holds, two final-turn assaults and zero failed direct advances.

The strategic results confirm that the rule improves the attempt rather than guaranteeing victory. One run had several armies converge on launched England and Native America captured and razed London on turn 247, canceling England's Space victory. In the final save-file 450 confirmation, Delhi was captured and razed on turn 265, Timbuktu was captured and razed on turn 279, and London had already been captured on turn 254. Native America still won Space from Cahokia on turn 291: nearby Egyptian groups had only 58% and 21% immediate strength, while a stronger 24-unit final assault could not finish the city. The AI now pursues the only target that can stop a launched spaceship, moves there without wasting the countdown, gathers strength when time permits and still makes the desperate attempt when necessary, but a well-defended Space victory can legitimately survive.

Fixed/improved with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex) thanks.

<a id="ki-191"></a>

## KI#191 - (Fixed/Improved) Base AdvCiv UWAI issue: independent target rolls could reject the best war target and then select a much worse rival

Base AdvCiv UWAI ranked eligible rivals, but then rolled separately for each one until a roll succeeded. This mixed two different decisions: whether the AI was willing to prepare any war and which rival was strategically best. If the preferred target failed its roll, a much weaker later candidate could still succeed by chance.

The clearest save-file 450 example occurred on turn 215. China rated Ethiopia at 68% war drive, distance 4 and 51% of China's power; England at 7%, distance 5 and 59% power; and India at only 5%, distance 11 and 38% power. The first two rolls failed and the third succeeded, so China prepared against faraway India despite rating nearby Ethiopia far higher.

With `SAS_UWAI_ONLY_ROLL_BEST_ELIGIBLE_WAR_TARGET_ENABLE` enabled, UWAI now finds the highest final adjusted drive after its existing eligibility, personality, and local-target checks, then rolls only that target. If the roll fails, the AI does not prepare a war that turn instead of falling through to a rival it judged worse. The personality roll therefore still decides whether to begin a war preparation, but random chance no longer substitutes an inferior target. Disabling the define restores the inherited independent rolls.

Confirming runs of save files 450 and 452 selected the highest final-drive target in all 81 successful decisions, with zero mismatches. Save file 450 also contained nine failed best-target rolls with another logged candidate available; the AI correctly declined the inferior alternatives, including 27% against 3%, 39% against 1%, and 29% against 4%. Warfare remained active, with 21 wars and 25 city captures in save file 450 and 28 wars and 24 city captures in save file 452.

Fixed/improved with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex) thanks.

<a id="ki-192"></a>

## KI#192 - (Fixed/Improved) Base AdvCiv/K-Mod island Worker logistics and AdvCiv-SAS production safety gap could strand Workers and other land civilians where they had no use

Screenshots/files for this issue: [google drive folder link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1b_GCvJycwz2WjAs71zEwQRD9D6SMhciV?usp=sharing).

Save-file 450 screenshots and SASGameRecord logging exposed land civilian units that could not do their assigned job on isolated landmasses. The clearest example was a Worker that accompanied the Settler to the island where Thapsus was founded, then remained idle there for 93 turns because none of its plots could be improved. This wastes a useful Worker, transport capacity, movement and maintenance, while the Worker could instead improve the main empire. The same underlying production gap could also let an isolated city train a land Explorer after its landmass was already explored, or a land Spy with no rival city it could reach and no Spy transport available.

The inherited Worker handling had several separate causes. A Settler transport unloaded accompanying Workers at the destination without checking whether that landmass needed any. `AI_ferryWorkers` could keep selecting a small island city after enough Workers were already there. The Base AdvCiv Worker reserve calculation also rounded an extra future Worker contribution upward even when the city had no unimproved same-landmass plot that a Worker could improve. Finally, higher-level production normally checked local demand, but different production routes and substitutions did not share one final area-usefulness veto.

The cure now checks the destination landmass's exact unmet Worker demand before unloading founding cargo. At the initial departure, Workers beyond that shortage remain in the origin city; at the destination, only the required number unload and any excess stays aboard for reuse elsewhere. As a safety guard, origin unloading is allowed only before the founding mission begins, so reconsidering the voyage in another friendly city cannot leave Workers there without evaluating that city's needs. A Worker left on its origin landmass refuses to reboard the same founding transport while it still targets that no-demand landmass. Worker ferrying treats the destination landmass's calculated need as a hard capacity. These checks compare current need with the current Worker count, so production and delivery become eligible again if losses leave the landmass short or new work raises its need.

Immediately before ordinary AI unit production is committed, `CvCityAI::AI_chooseUnit` now applies one central area-usefulness gate after all substitutions have resolved the final `UnitAI`. It refuses a land Worker when the landmass already has enough Workers, a land Explorer when existing Explorers meet the remaining exploration need, and a land Spy in a secondary isolated colony with neither a known rival city on that landmass nor an adjacent Spy transport. The primary landmass remains allowed to produce Spies so an overseas empire can still create Spies and their transports. Free or scripted units and the human production governor remain separate because this is an AI strategic production decision rather than a game-rule restriction.

The first therapeutic run confirmed that our initial cure correctly made founding transports leave unnecessary Workers on their large origin landmass, but also revealed the remaining layers: general Worker logic kept loading one of those Workers back onto its island-bound Settler transport, causing the transport to unload the same Worker onto the origin landmass 14 times. Even after that loop was stopped, a separate Worker-ferry routine continued sending extra Workers to islands that already had enough, accumulating 1 Worker on Bactra's one-tile landmass, 5 on Sardis's two-tile landmass and 2 on Ergili's three-tile landmass, where most had no useful work.

After correcting the reserve, reboarding and ferry-cap paths, the final `BBAI_20260720T103610Z_load1.log` recorded only one Worker left on its origin landmass: its destination needed 1 Worker but already had 3, so this was correct. It never reboarded. No invalid Worker, Explorer or Spy request reached the central gate in that run because the corrected demand logic prevented those candidates earlier; the central gate remains the final protection for unusual production paths.

The follow-up cure also addresses Workers that were genuinely needed when delivered but later completed every useful task. Base AdvCiv forced every revealed landmass above 3 tiles to retain at least 1 Worker, so a completed secondary island never reached zero demand; owned cities also caused the stranded-unit logic to reject its Worker from naval rescue. The primary landmass still keeps this reserve, but a completed secondary landmass can now reach zero Worker demand. Only after ordinary Worker logic finds no productive local action, the Worker moves to a suitable coast, advertises itself for pickup and waits there. An available empty Settler transport can collect it without interrupting an active founding mission. The first transport assignment reserves that individual Worker so additional ships remain available for other duties or other completed-area Workers.

The completed-secondary-landmass rule does not apply to Barbarians. Their separate islands do not use the normal civilization system that collects a finished Worker and reassigns it to another landmass. In addition, a Barbarian city's best-build cache can remain empty until it has a Worker; without the inherited local reserve, both the area and city calculations can report zero Worker demand, so `AI_barbChooseProduction` never produces the Worker needed to reveal and perform those local jobs.

Barbarians therefore keep the inherited local Worker reserve in both calculations, while ordinary civilizations retain the completed-secondary-landmass behavior above. In the confirming `BBAI_20260720T193721Z_load1.log`, Barbarian cities completed 13 Workers across 11 cities, preserving their ability to develop their separate islands.

The confirming `BBAI_20260720T150846Z_load1.log` recorded 14 completed-area Worker boardings. Persia recovered all 5 Workers from its completed islands on turn 226, including 2 that boarded available transports directly and 3 collected through the stranded-unit pickup path. No two distinct transports targeted the same Worker during the same turn after the coordination guard. If no empty transport is available, the Worker waits rather than forcing the AI to build a ship or divert one carrying useful cargo solely for that rescue. Worker demand rises normally again if losses, new technology, expansion or other changes create useful work on the landmass.

Update (AdvCiv-SAS 6565): the XML-driven Worker tests exposed the complementary case: a city can own a useful BFC plot on a different land area from its city tile. The Archipelago sample's Tianjin retained its only non-city land plot unimproved through turn 350 because city Worker demand and ordinary path checks treated that small island as inaccessible rather than actionable.

`AI_bestCityBuild` can now evaluate exactly one such off-area BFC plot without pretending a land path already exists; when the plot has a worthwhile legal Build, maritime Worker transport can deliver a Worker. Once that isolated area has no remaining useful job, the existing completed-area evacuation path can recover it. An analogous one-land-plot Arpinum received a Workshop immediately in the follow-up run, while finished islands still return to zero demand instead of accumulating spare Workers.

Fixed/improved with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex) thanks.

## KI#193 - (Fixed/Improved) Base AdvCiv/K-Mod generic army thresholds could make loaded assault ships wait instead of taking achievable overseas targets

Screenshots/files for this issue: [google drive folder link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ipCkOvU21QPGlYY-WvGtfh-LlXCpNqfz?usp=sharing).

The new overseas-transport BBAI diagnostics exposed a Base AdvCiv/K-Mod mismatch between assembling an army and deciding whether a loaded fleet could take a specific city by sea. This includes separate-island targets and coastal landings elsewhere on the same continent. `AI_assaultSeaMove` normally waited for generic reinforcement or invasion sizes derived from the AI's broad city-assault army requirements. Those requirements could exceed the transport group's entire cargo capacity, so the fleet could never reach them without more ships. The existing `AI_assaultSeaTransport` target evaluator already compared the actual cargo's strength with the target's defenders, distance and other tactical conditions, but the generic threshold could prevent that more relevant evaluation from running.

Save file 450 showed the issue clearly. Persia's fleet consisted of one Galley with 3 total cargo spaces, but the generic thresholds required 13 units before carrying reinforcements to an overseas attack already under way or 26 units before launching its own full invasion. The fleet could not reach either threshold unless more transports joined it. The same problem applies whenever all ships in a fleet together cannot carry its required generic army size. Nearby Barbarian cities later reached zero defenders, including Mycenian on turn 237 and Hittite on turn 271, but the fleet still alternated between waiting, loading and unloading instead of exploiting the opportunity; Hittite eventually changed owner through culture rather than conquest.

With `SAS_AI_ASSAULT_SEA_OPPORTUNISTIC_TARGET_ENABLE` enabled, a naval assault group that has military cargo but remains below its generic army-assembly threshold now asks the existing target-specific evaluator whether that cargo can already capture a real target. This check runs only after the inherited safety, escort and imminent-loading waits, and it does not lower the normal thresholds used to organize major invasions. A small fleet therefore departs when its actual strength is sufficient for the city it can reach, but continues gathering units when the available targets are too strong.

The naval evaluator now also applies the shared distant-disposable Barbarian-city safeguard from KI#188.5 using its already-computed sea path. A fleet does not sail far away merely to raze a city and clear the site for a nearer rival; it can still attack a nearby opportunity or a city that `AI_isSASCityLikelyToBenefitUsLongTerm` says is worth keeping. An otherwise worthwhile isolated-island foothold is not rejected merely for being on another landmass: the same-area distance limit applies only when the AI already owns a city on that target landmass.

The save-file 450 confirming run recorded 7 distinct below-threshold fleets finding a valid target, while 76 other evaluations found no acceptable target and correctly kept their fleets waiting. The changed history produced 6 additional Barbarian-city conquests: Mycenian, Circassian, Cherokee, Cimmerian, Harappan and Sakae; none was razed. Maya provided the clearest example: 2 cargo units departed despite a generic threshold of 7 and captured population-9 Thracian on the next turn, then a 4-unit cargo captured Mycenian eight turns later.

Save file 449 independently confirmed the behavior on another island-rich map. India sent 3 units despite a threshold of 9 and captured the Barbarian island city Burgundian six turns later. The cure also applies to coastal troop transport rather than only isolated islands: a separate 2-unit Indian launch supported the capture of the Ottoman city Ankara through a coastal landing five turns later, and a 4-unit Byzantine landing despite a threshold of 10 supported the capture of the English city Hastings on the next turn.

The run also recorded 28 other below-threshold evaluations that found no acceptable target and kept their fleets waiting, showing that the new path does not launch every partially loaded ship. India remained the strongest civilization and won by Space, so these smaller expeditions did not prevent it from maintaining its broader strength.

This cure does not solve a separate production-capacity issue found by the same diagnostics: Mali had a 15-18-unit attack army but only one already-full capacity-3 assault transport, while Carthage had attack groups of 18 and 21 without a geographically eligible assault transport. Whether land-heavy-map production limits leave some profitable islands without enough transport capacity remains a separate investigation.

Fixed/improved with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex) thanks.

<a id="ki-193.2"></a>

## KI#193.2 - (Fixed SAS transport-accounting defect) Dual-coast ports omitted docked assault-transport capacity

Queue-005 WIP283 found that the repaired selected-water-area capacity count could omit transports docked through a dual-coast city's other adjacent water area. The original overproduction fix remained useful, but its topology coverage was incomplete.

Update: the completed repair shares one dual-coast predicate with the naval-trade correction in KI#197.6. A docked assault transport now belongs to the selected sea when either the port's primary accessible water area or `secondWaterArea()` matches it, so capacity on the opposite coast is no longer omitted or needlessly replaced.

The repaired DLL compiled successfully, and a water-rich full autoplay completed without an observed production or runtime issue.

This is the production-side follow-up to KI#193. That cure lets an existing loaded fleet consider a specific achievable target before reaching Base AdvCiv/K-Mod's generic invasion size, but the same overseas-transport diagnostics showed that an AI could know a worthwhile nearby island city and have ample attackers without producing the ship needed to carry them there.

Base AdvCiv's invasion-production branch mainly requested assault transports when the current area was already classified for an overseas assault, or when no enemy city at all could be reached by land. This created two mismatches:

- an unrelated enemy city reachable by land could suppress transport demand even when another nearby overseas city was a better opportunity;
- the available land army itself could raise general military spending above the invasion-production limit, so having enough attackers made the missing transport less likely to be produced.

Save file 450 demonstrated the latter clearly. Carthage had 24 available attackers against only 1 defender in Cimmerian, which was 9 plots from its nearest Carthaginian city, but no eligible assault transport. In the diagnostic run, Cimmerian remained Barbarian until turn 246. Other cases included Mali having a 15-18-unit attack army but only one already-full capacity-3 Galley, and Carthaginian attack groups of 18 and 21 without a geographically usable assault transport.

With `SAS_AI_ASSAULT_SEA_OPPORTUNISTIC_PRODUCTION_ENABLE` enabled, a safe coastal city now searches for a limited missing-lift opportunity before the inherited broad invasion branch. A candidate must be revealed and reachable through the city's water area. A non-Barbarian city must belong to a rival the AI is already at war with or preparing to attack, while a Barbarian city remains available without declaring war. The target must pass `AI_isSASCityLikelyToBenefitUsLongTerm`, have positive city-target value, lie within the XML-tunable distance from the nearest owned city, and have enough available land attackers to plausibly overcome its current defenders.

The request is deliberately bounded rather than a general naval mobilization:

- it asks only for cargo space appropriate to the available attackers and target defenders;
- real transports at sea or docked in a connected port count by their actual cargo space, and ships currently being trained count by their expected cargo space;
- once enough existing or queued capacity is found, other cities do not duplicate the request;
- financial trouble, city danger and a defensive area cancel the opportunity;
- the central `AI_chooseUnit` production limits still apply, preventing this path from bypassing the AdvCiv-SAS safeguards against naval overproduction;
- the default maximum nearest-city distance is 18 plots, so the AI does not build a new fleet solely for a faraway prize. Existing transports remain free to exploit such a target through the normal logic when that is worthwhile.

The first save-file 450 implementation exposed an accounting error: a transport docked in a coastal city occupies the city's land plot, so checking only whether the ship was in the water area missed it. Cities could therefore request another transport immediately after the first order was accepted. Counting docked ships and ships already being trained fixed this: evaluations recognizing existing or queued capacity rose from 0 to 95, decisions finding enough capacity rose from 25 to 95, successful opportunistic orders fell from 9 to 7, and the duplicate late Arabian requests disappeared.

The final save-file 450 run did not revive the old naval overproduction. Ordinary AI assault fleets reached at most 3 ships. Cimmerian was captured on turn 199 instead of turn 246 in the diagnostic run, Hittite on turn 218 instead of 256, and Harappan on turn 242 instead of 262; all 5 tracked Barbarian cities had been captured by turn 242.

Save file 449 independently tested the cure on another island-rich but land-heavy map. Across 456 turns, 140 evaluations correctly found enough existing capacity and only 7 opportunistic transport orders were accepted; ordinary AI assault fleets peaked at 4 ships, far below the old 10-20-transport failure. The original Minoan opportunity did not recur because the history diverged, but the changed city on that site was captured using existing transport capacity. Hannibal also captured faraway Illinois using one existing Galleon and 4 units: because the nearest Carthaginian city was 27 plots away, beyond the default production limit of 18, that profitable small expedition did not cause the AI to build a new fleet for the distant target.

Chehalis changing from Mali in the older run to Aztec ownership in this confirming run was unrelated to the cure because it was reachable by land. Both runs valued the city as worthwhile. In the older history, Aztec remained committed to a costly Scandinavian war while Mali made peace and reached Chehalis first; in the confirming history, the Aztec war ended earlier and its freed army captured Chehalis before Mali. This is useful evidence that preserving available military tempo matters, but not evidence that the overseas-production rule selected Chehalis.

The original fix was implemented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex); its dual-coast omission was reopened through ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's Queue-005 WIP283 audit and completed with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#194 - (Fixed SAS overseas-settlement defect) A capital omitted Settler sites reachable through its second water area

Queue-005 WIP282 found that the central Settler water-area repair checks the capital's primary adjacent sea but omits `secondWaterArea()`. An isthmus or dual-coast capital can therefore miss worthwhile islands reachable through its other sea.

The overseas-settlement diagnostics added after KI#193.2 exposed an AdvCiv-SAS regression introduced accidentally by KI#181's otherwise useful weak-site Settler-production floor. KI#181 added `SAS_getSettlerBuildSiteStatus` as the final guard before a concrete Settler order, but its water-site check copied only the producing city's directly relevant water area and omitted an inherited K-Mod/AdvCiv fallback used by the surrounding production logic. In save file 449, India knew a valuable nearby Fish/Whale/Crab island site at `(39,10)` and already had 2 Settler transports with 6 total cargo space. The inherited `CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction` logic could see the island, but because Delhi was inland, the new AdvCiv-SAS gate received a null water area, repeatedly reported `hasBuildSite=0 waterSites=0` from turns 119-129, and rejected the Settler despite the reachable island opportunity.

The mismatch meant India did not produce the Settler for that island. It eventually founded Varanasi on the same plot only on turn 171, after an unrelated land city site made the general Settler gate pass. Thus a useful existing transport network and a worthwhile island could remain unused merely because the capital itself was inland.

The new shared `SAS_getSettlerWaterArea` keeps the normal directly relevant water area for a coastal city. When the producing city has none, it uses the map's largest water area only if the player already has a `UNITAI_SETTLER_SEA` transport there. Both the broad production logic and the final concrete Settler gate now use this same result. The existing-transport requirement prevents an inland capital from treating an inaccessible overseas site as immediately buildable, while allowing it to use shipping capacity it already possesses.

The first confirming save-file 449 run logged the corrected decision on turn 119: `hasBuildSite=1 areaSites=0 waterSites=2 waterBest=2003`, against the configured early Settler floor of 2000. Delhi immediately selected the Settler and founded Varanasi at `(39,10)` on turn 128, 43 turns earlier than the diagnostic run and without waiting for an unrelated land site. A second run independently founded Varanasi on turn 117, then produced another Settler for the next qualifying island site.

That second Settler exposed the separate KI#179 follow-up described there: it reached a danger-free valid site but the existing escort safeguard prevented it from founding. After narrowing only direct danger-free founding, the final run founded Agra immediately on turn 144 instead of turn 257. Save file 450 then confirmed that the original dangerous-expansion protection remained guarded. Together, the tests show that the AI can exploit worthwhile islands from an inland capital without restoring reckless dangerous founding.

Update: the shared Settler-water helper now evaluates both unique strategically relevant seas adjacent to the producing city and selects the coast with the strongest known Settler site, breaking equal-value ties by site count. The inland-city fallback remains unchanged: only the largest sea is considered, and only when the player already owns a Settler transport there. Both broad production planning and the final concrete Settler gate consume the same selected area and already-computed site values. The repaired DLL compiled successfully, and a water-rich full autoplay completed without an observed production or runtime issue.

The original fix/improvement was implemented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex); its second-coast omission was reopened through ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's Queue-005 WIP282 audit and fixed with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

<a id="ki-195"></a>

## KI#195 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv/K-Mod omission and SAS repair defect) Barbarian Work Boat demand used incomplete city-radius and availability scopes

Queue-005 WIP292 found that the earlier outer-radius diagnosis and repair relied on a helper whose actual plot coverage did not match the assumed contract. The Work Boat counting cure needs to be rebuilt from the real city-radius and seafood-demand scopes.

Screenshots/files for this issue: [google drive folder link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1tchRI0bVg3IlT2n6BjyciLXnEW1JML4P?usp=sharing).

Save-file 450 repeatedly showed Barbarian seafood remaining unimproved. The new level-3 Work Boat audit confirmed that this was primarily a production failure rather than a movement failure: Barbarians owned up to 11 seafood bonuses at once, and many safe, buildable and reachable targets remained unassigned for 100-163 turns. Across 22 distinct audited targets, 16 were assigned to Barbarian cities and 12 of those were in the outer city radius, yet Barbarians produced only 2 Work Boats. Both boats immediately improved their intended adjacent Molluscs, showing that their movement and improvement logic worked once a boat existed.

Direct comparison with Base AdvCiv 1.12 confirmed the first cause in its `advc.305` Barbarian branch of `CvCityAI::AI_neededSeaWorkers`. Although the comment says each Barbarian city should train Work Boats for its own needs, `FOR_EACH_ADJ_PLOT` checked only the eight plots immediately beside the city. It therefore ignored the outer part of the normal workable city radius. AdvCiv-SAS preserves the useful city-local policy but checks every owned water plot assigned to that city, and counts it only when the appropriate sea improvement can currently be built and reached.

The first confirming run improved 13 of 14 seafood targets assigned to a Barbarian city; the remaining city was conquered before completion. However, it also exposed a second related Base AdvCiv mismatch. `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` finds docked and queued ships by iterating major-civilization cities, so the Base Barbarian production branch did not count Work Boats waiting inside or being trained by Barbarian cities. Hun consequently ordered boats repeatedly for the same remaining targets, and Barbarians accumulated as many as 20 Work Boats at once.

The final cure counts Work Boats already sailing in the relevant water area, plus those docked or being trained in the current Barbarian city. It does not let boats in unrelated Barbarian cities suppress valid local production. In the final confirming run, the peak fell from 20 Work Boats to 2 while 12 city-assigned seafood targets were improved. The other 3 assigned targets belonged to Shangian or Visigoth; both cities produced or assigned Work Boats but were conquered before the improvements could finish. Owned seafood outside every Barbarian city's workable assignment remains a separate possible policy enhancement rather than being included in this city-local fix.

Update: Queue-005 WIP292 verified that the full assigned-city-radius demand loop above is correct, but disproved the second repair's helper assumption. `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` scans every alive player's cities, including Barbarian cities, so it already counted the current city's docked/queued boat and also let another Barbarian city's docked/queued boat suppress this city's independent local demand. The completed correction instead uses `AI_totalAreaUnitAIs` for boats physically sailing in the accessible production sea, then adds only the current city's docked and queued boats explicitly. This matches the intended city-local demand contract and preserves the `waterArea(true)` Ice/accessibility edge case.

The repaired DLL compiled successfully, and a water-rich full autoplay with Barbarians enabled completed without an observed production or runtime issue.

The inherited outer-radius omission was fixed/improved with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex); the helper-contract defect in that SAS repair was reopened through ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's Queue-005 WIP292 audit and fixed with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

<a id="ki-196"></a>

## KI#196 - (Fixed/Improved) AdvCiv-SAS's short-chain irrigation replacement could leave valuable BFC bonus Farms dry for up to 191 turns (Base AdvCiv had a similar untargeted routine, which AdvCiv-SAS does not use because it conflicted with SAS improvement choice)

Base AdvCiv did contain `CvUnitAI::AI_irrigateTerritory`, but it did not plan an irrigation chain toward a city plot. It scanned owned plots outside every city's workable assignment, considered only plots that could already receive irrigation from fresh water or an adjacent irrigated plot, and chose mainly by the Worker's travel distance. It could therefore extend irrigation incidentally one Farm at a time, but it did not know which dry Farm or city it was helping. AdvCiv-SAS had functionally disabled this broad routine because it could spend Worker turns creating irrigation-carrying Farms without a concrete city need and interfere with our deliberate Cottage, Workshop and Farm choices.

The first AdvCiv-SAS replacement was more purposeful because it started from a dry Farm or a low-food city plot, but it was only a short local heuristic. It searched at most four plots from the target, selected a plausible connector without retaining an end-to-end route, and excluded bonus plots from its dry-Farm targets. BBAI logging exposed the clearest result in save file 450: Mayapan's Maize already had a Farm but remained dry from turn 121 through turn 312, a span of 191 turns, despite an achievable owned route to irrigation.

The completed cure searches for a deterministic least-cost route across adjacent owned flat farmable plots from each actual dry BFC Farm to currently available irrigation. Farm-specific bonuses are valid targets. The Worker builds the source-side missing Farm first, then recalculates after each completed link so newly carried irrigation advances along the route toward the intended target.

Existing Farms and owned flat cities can carry the route without being rebuilt. The route cost favors fewer plots and penalizes replacing Workshops, matured growth improvements and other existing improvements; bonus plots and automation-protected improvements are not used as new connectors. `SAS_WORKER_AI_IRRIGATION_CHAIN_MAX_PLOTS`, 12 by default, prevents the AI from replacing improvements across an excessive part of its empire for one target.

In the confirming save-file 450 run, the route toward Mayapan's Maize advanced on turns 121, 128, 138, 149 and 160; after turn 162, the dry-Farm diagnostic stopped. Najran and Elephantine remained dry because the detailed route search confirmed that water, hills and unowned or foreign plots genuinely blocked every owned farmable route rather than because the Worker forgot an achievable chain.

Save file 449 independently confirmed a long route to Camulodunum's Rice: its Farm was irrigated by turn 206 and remained so until an enemy pillaged it on turn 319. Ollantaytambo initially had no owned route, then its border expansion made one valid on turn 152 and Workers completed it by turn 176.

Save file 452 produced 110 selected irrigation-chain jobs; valid routes used at most 7 plots, so none reached the default maximum of 12. The only five repeated target/location failures were explained by current ownership or terrain, and Avar's later repeated dry Farm was a pillaged improvement that Workers repaired before its diagnostic stopped again.

### Update (AdvCiv-SAS 6565)

The Worker refactor retains this deterministic route planner but removes Farm as its C++ representative. Candidate carriers and dry targets now come from every improvement whose loaded XML sets `bCarriesIrrigation`; the route follows actual irrigation availability and resulting yields, and its special overwrite protection applies only to a completed carrier or a carrier currently useful to the concrete route.

Configured growth-improvement overwrite costs follow XML `ImprovementUpgrade` chains rather than naming Cottage/Hamlet/Village/Town. The present AdvCiv-SAS XML still normally produces Farm chains, but modmods can add, remove or rebalance food, production or commerce irrigation carriers without adding another identity branch to this code or SASGameRecord revision 124's matching territory report.

### Update 2 (AdvCiv-SAS 6572)

Later level-3 Worker diagnostics found a second defect in this **AdvCiv-SAS chain system itself**. The deterministic route planner could correctly build a source-side carrier and advance toward its target, but ordinary `AI_bestCityBuild` yield valuation could then replace that upstream carrier before the downstream link was secure.

In Barcelona, a flat city tile also bridged the dependency, which the older adjacent-carrier protection did not model. The result was a repeated SAS-created Farm/Workshop loop even though the route search itself was valid.

The repair protects both kinds of live SAS route dependency without reverting to Base AdvCiv's untargeted irrigation routine. While a viable chain still needs its next source-side step, currently irrigated carriers supplying that step are protected from ordinary non-carrier replacement.

For already established chains, the Worker AI tests the remaining potential-irrigation connected component with the candidate source removed; if an owned downstream XML carrier would otherwise have no surviving fresh-water source, the provider remains protected. Flat city tiles can therefore bridge a real dependency, while a carrier with another surviving source or a no-longer-needed connector remains replaceable.

A controlled Tiny Islands replay validated the cure. Through turn 370, Barcelona `(8,63)` direct reversals fell from 55 to 1, cross-path reversals from 67 to 17, reversals within five turns from 86 to 34, total reversals from 146 to 111, and replacement assignments from 587 to 486. `SASGameRecord` remained identical through turn 151 and first diverged on turn 152, exactly when the new city-bridged provider protection first changed gameplay.

The run then completed normally by Space Race. Remaining rapid Farm/Workshop reversals caused entirely by ordinary `CITY_BUILD` scarcity weighting are tracked separately; this irrigation fix deliberately does not mask them with a generic replacement cooldown.

Fixed/improved with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol (on ChatGPT Codex) thanks.

## KI#197 - (Fixed SAS military-production improvement defect) Power-per-city catch-up counted vassal power but not vassal cities

Queue-005 WIP286 found that the improved under-strength catch-up numerator includes vassal power while its per-city denominator omits vassal cities. This mismatched empire scope can overstate military weakness and production demand.

Update: SAS's catch-up now counts every relevant rival master's vassal cities alongside the master cities before dividing the already coalition-wide `getPower(true)` numerator. The rival power-per-city average therefore uses one consistent coalition scope, while the inherited total-power throttle and SAS's own-team `getPower(false)` / team-city pair remain unchanged.

The repaired DLL compiled successfully, and a full autoplay completed without an observed production or runtime issue.

Screenshots/files for this issue: [google drive folder link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12ausI-H34CWK1jaXzn1cedb0l9yOvxtX?usp=sharing).

The dedicated `SAS_BBAI_MILITARY_PRODUCTION_LOG_LEVEL` diagnostics were added to investigate AI military production, notably to investigate why some AIs produced very large armies while others remained comparatively weak. Before reaching the inherited issue documented here, that investigation first exposed two AdvCiv-SAS-specific problems. The SAS no-production safety net treated a valid Process as if the city had no production, so an AI that rejected another unit because of its normal military-spending limit could deliberately choose Wealth, Research or another Process and then have that Process immediately replaced by a forced military unit. That was fixed by limiting the fallback to genuinely empty or invalid production queues. The same investigation also showed that SASGameRecord's old `militaryUnits` field used `CvPlayer::getNumMilitaryUnits()`, which counts XML `bMilitarySupport` units rather than all combat-capable units; the log now records `combatUnits` and `militarySupportUnits` separately. These were AdvCiv-SAS-specific findings already fixed before this issue and are only context for how the remaining Base AdvCiv behavior was isolated.

After those confounders were removed, the logs showed a remaining asymmetry inherited directly from Base AdvCiv/K-Mod in `CvCityAI::AI_buildUnitProb`. The existing relative-power logic identifies relevant rivals and reduces unit-production probability once the AI's total power is clearly above its target relative to the strongest relevant rival. There is no corresponding upward adjustment when the AI is weak relative to the size of its own empire. A civilization that expands quickly can therefore acquire many cities faster than its army grows and remain under-militarized for its size while ordinary building and unit-production logic continues without a relative-power catch-up signal.

The logs showed this concretely in more than one game. In save file 458, Kublai reached 9 cities with 579 team power, about 64 power per city against a relevant-rival city-weighted average of about 125; the inherited logic had no upward response to that deficit. In save file 457, Shaka independently reached 7 cities with 377 power, about 54 per city against a relevant-rival average of about 94. These were not simply small empires failing to match a much larger rival's raw army total: they were empires whose military density had fallen well behind the field as they expanded.

AdvCiv-SAS now adds a bounded adjustment in the opposite direction. It compares the AI team's power per city with the city-weighted average power per city of the same relevant rivals already considered by the inherited relative-power logic. Using power per city avoids telling a small empire to match a much larger rival's total army, while using the city-weighted rival average avoids letting one unusually militarized small rival dominate the target. The increase scales with the relative power-per-city deficit up to `SAS_AI_BUILD_UNIT_PROB_UNDERSTRENGTH_POWER_PER_CITY_MAX_BOOST_PERCENT`, 50% by default.

The catch-up remains inside the normal `AI_buildUnitProb` path rather than forcing a unit order. It does not apply when the existing logic has already greatly reduced military production for financial/economic reasons, while the AI is deliberately waiting for better units, when war is impossible, or when the inherited total-power logic already says the AI is clearly strong enough and is throttling production. The resulting `iBuildUnitProb` still flows through the ordinary spending limits, building choices, UnitAI selection and concrete-unit checks.

Save file 458 produced two independent refined full runs with very similar behavior despite divergent game histories. The catch-up fired in 2,765 of 5,839 build-probability evaluations (about 47%) in one run and 2,542 of 5,501 (about 46%) in the rerun. The average requested increases were about +17%, corresponding to about +7 actual BuildUnitProb points, and neither run contained a case where the under-strength boost fired together with the inherited high-power throttle. Save file 457 independently reproduced the same pattern with a different leader set and RNG state: 2,152 of 4,674 evaluations (about 46%) were boosted, averaging about +19% and about +9 actual BuildUnitProb points, again with zero boost/throttle conflicts.

In practical terms, the correction made the ordinary AI production logic noticeably more military-biased whenever an empire's army density lagged behind relevant rivals: when active, it raised BuildUnitProb by about 7 to 9 percentage points on average, making affected cities more likely to continue toward unit production through the normal production gates. This does not mean 7 to 9% more units overall because spending limits, building choices, UnitAI selection and concrete-unit checks still apply; it means under-strength AIs now receive a consistent catch-up pressure that Base AdvCiv lacked.

The runs also retained substantial variation between civilizations rather than equalizing every army. Small empires were evaluated by military density rather than being asked to chase the raw total power of much larger rivals, while rapidly expanded empires could receive strong temporary pressure until their military caught up. The earlier SAS Process-fallback overproduction did not return: the refined runs continued to show only genuine empty-queue fallback contexts and no Process-replacement fallback.

A separate related Base AdvCiv/K-Mod follow-up was also exposed by the same diagnostics: `AI_chooseProduction` short-circuit 2 explicitly lowers building odds as `iBuildUnitProb` rises, while the later short-circuit 3 did not use `iBuildUnitProb`. That distinct issue is addressed in KI#197.2. Continued production-branch auditing then exposed the separate spending and role-selection issues documented in KI#197.3 through KI#197.6, followed by the earlier building-gate issue documented in KI#197.7.

The original improvement was implemented with the help of ChatGPT-5.6-Sol; its coalition-scope mismatch was reopened through ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's Queue-005 WIP286 audit and fixed with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#197.2 - (Fixed/Improved) Base AdvCiv/K-Mod final building short-circuit (`CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction`'s short-circuit 3) ignored BuildUnitProb and could override strong military-production pressure immediately before generic unit production

The dedicated military-production diagnostics used for KI#197 exposed a second inherited issue in `CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction`. Short-circuit 2 already lowers building odds as `iBuildUnitProb` rises, but short-circuit 3 - the final "last chance to catch important buildings" immediately before generic unit production - recalculated its building chance from building value and land-war state alone. Strong military-production pressure could therefore survive the earlier production logic and then be partly forgotten at the final building retry.

This was repeatable across the pre-fix logs. During severe under-strength (`understrengthBoostPercent >= 40`), short-circuit 3 chose its building in 7 of 9 and 7 of 8 evaluated cases in two save-file 458 runs, and 15 of 25 cases in save file 457. A concrete save-file 457 example was Shaka's Nobamba at turn 185: `BuildUnitProb` was 84 and short-circuit 2 gave the Grocer only 8% odds, but the inherited short-circuit 3 formula restored a 52% building chance immediately before the generic unit gate.

AdvCiv-SAS now keeps that last building chance, but proportionally reduces its base odds with the AI's already-computed `iBuildUnitProb`. `SAS_AI_CHOOSE_PRODUCTION_SHORT_CIRCUIT_3_BUILD_UNIT_PROB_WEIGHT_PERCENT`, 50 by default, controls how strongly that military pressure applies; for example, `BuildUnitProb=80` with the default weight reduces short-circuit 3 base building odds by 40%. Existing production-progress preference inside `AI_chooseBuilding` is unchanged, so an important building that is already underway still retains its normal continuity advantage. Setting the define to 0 restores the inherited Base AdvCiv/K-Mod short-circuit 3 odds.

The first test version applied this reduction whenever `iBuildUnitProb` was high, but save file 458 exposed that this was too broad. At turn 119 Aachen already had unit spending 102 against the generic gate's `max+15` allowance of 99, yet the prototype still reduced a Forge from 32% to 25%; when the Forge roll then failed, a later inherited city-counter exception produced an Axeman despite the ordinary spending gate already saying that generic unit production was over budget. The final version therefore applies the short-circuit 3 reduction only while the same normal `+15` military-spending gate would still allow another generic unit. In the confirming rerun, the turn-119 Aachen case remained at 32% and chose the Forge, matching the pre-SC3 branch.

The refined save-file 458 run evaluated short-circuit 3 640 times. 375 evaluations were already above the relevant spending allowance and were left completely unchanged; only the 265 cases with spending headroom could receive the new reduction. Among severe under-strength cases, 25 still had spending room: their average short-circuit 3 building chance fell from 48.4% to 32.9%, and the building was chosen in 5 of those 25 cases. The other 15 severe cases were already over the spending threshold and retained Base AdvCiv odds. The first causal divergence from the old save-file 458 branch moved from the over-budget Aachen case to turn 128 Vienne, where unit spending was 0 against a normal maximum of 98 and `BuildUnitProb` was 51; the Buddhist Monastery's final building chance fell from 52% to 39%, after which the city eventually chose a Spearman.

The earlier save-file 457 prototype test also supported the intended direction: severe short-circuit 3 building choices fell from 15 of 25 in the old run to 11 of 27 after weighting. Retrospectively, 24 of the 25 old severe save-file 457 cases had the spending headroom required by the final refinement, so the added spending gate preserves almost all of the target correction while avoiding unrelated pressure once the AI is already over its normal unit budget.

Fixed/improved with the help of ChatGPT-5.6-Sol thanks.

## KI#197.3 - (Fixed/Improved) Base AdvCiv/K-Mod late floating-defender retry ignored military unit-spending limits and could keep producing extra defenders far above budget in peace

Screenshots/files for this issue: [google drive folder link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_X49NMplPbGxRBoroNTki2ky1kl6HiJ2?usp=sharing).

The continued KI#197 military-production audit exposed a separate inherited spending inconsistency in `CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction`. Base AdvCiv/K-Mod has an earlier floating-defender pass that checks unit spending before adding more defenders, but the later 50% retry (the branch logged as `choose floating defender 2`) only checked whether the AI was short of floating defenders and whether financial trouble or land war allowed the branch. It had no military-spending check. Direct comparison with Base AdvCiv 1.13 confirmed that this late retry is inherited rather than introduced by AdvCiv-SAS.

The effect was repeatable across several pre-fix full runs. In save file 457, 153 of 281 actual floating-defender-2 choices occurred at or above the normal `max+15` military-spending allowance; 97 of those 153 were peaceful rather than land-war cases. Save file 456 had 85 of 243 choices above `max+15`, including 70 peaceful cases, and a refined save-file 458 run had 49 of 270, including 44 peaceful cases. Many were only small composition shortages. One extreme save-file 456 example had Persia at 6 floating defenders against 7 wanted while unit spending was already 220 against a normal maximum of 84, yet the late retry still produced another military unit.

The first cure simply required the same `max+15` spending headroom used by later generic military production unless the AI was in a land war. That stopped the ordinary peaceful overspending, but the first save-file 456 rerun exposed the opposite edge case: a large army can still have a genuinely poor defensive composition. Eight blocked peaceful cases were severely short of floating defenders; for example, Persia later had only 8 floating defenders against 21 wanted while unit spending was only slightly above the threshold. A blanket budget veto would therefore fix overproduction at the cost of sometimes preventing useful composition repair.

The final rule keeps the spending gate but adds a narrow severe-shortage exception using the same threshold as the earlier floating-defender pass. Floating defender 2 can now ignore the `max+15` budget only during a land war or when floating defenders are severely below the requested count; an ordinary peaceful shortage must have spending headroom. This preserves the inherited role as a composition safety valve without allowing a one- or two-unit shortage to keep expanding an already oversized peaceful military.

The final save-file 456 validation logged 436 floating-defender-2 candidate states. 143 ordinary peaceful over-budget candidates were blocked, and no blocked candidate still produced through this branch. Eleven actual choices remained above `max+15`: 6 were severe peaceful shortages, 4 were land-war cases, and 1 qualified for both reasons. Save file 457 independently confirmed the same behavior. The old run had 153 of 281 actual choices above `max+15`; the final run had only 12 of 233, all explicitly explained by the intended exceptions (10 severe shortages and 2 land-war cases). Thus the branch remains active when composition really needs repair, while the broad peaceful spending bypass is removed.

Fixed/improved with the help of ChatGPT-5.6-Sol thanks.

<a id="ki-197.4"></a>

## KI#197.4 - (Fixed/Improved) AdvCiv-SAS excess-defender optimization could replace explicitly required `UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE` production with offensive UnitAIs, including minimum defenders and Settler escorts

The same production audit exposed an AdvCiv-SAS-specific interaction rather than a Base AdvCiv/K-Mod bug. `SAS_AI_CHOOSE_UNIT_NO_EXCESS_STRICT_DEFENDERS_UNITAIS` can redirect strict defensive UnitAI requests toward offense when the AI appears to have enough defenders. That optimization is useful for avoiding large passive defender stacks, but it was applied inside the broad concrete `AI_chooseUnit` path without knowing whether the caller had specifically determined that a `UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE` unit was required for a safety invariant.

This could make a safety branch request a real city defender and then return success after AdvCiv-SAS substituted an offensive role. The clearest logs were minimum-city-defense and Settler-escort cases. In one save-file 456 run, Pasargadae entered the minimum-defender branch and selected a Longbowman as `UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE`, but the SAS substitution changed the result to a Catapult with `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY`; the caller then logged that it had used the minimum-defender branch. Thebes repeatedly did the same while explicitly asking for defense for an existing Settler. Across the audited runs, 40-98 minimum-defender requests per run could be rewritten; in the last pre-fix save-file 456 sample, 98 of 322 minimum-defender requests were converted, including 49 while military spending was already above `max+15`.

An initial attempt guarded the substitution with `AI_countExcessDefenders`, but save-file testing showed that this metric is broader than the caller's actual requirement. It counts a general set of units that can help defend a city, whereas the minimum-defense branch is specifically comparing strict `UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE` coverage against `AI_minDefenders()` plus Settlers waiting for an escort. Under that first guard, 94 minimum-defender requests and 6 existing-Settler escort requests were still rewritten, so the approximation was discarded.

The final safeguard stays local to the existing SAS excess-defender optimization and leaves `AI_chooseUnit` signatures and production callers unchanged. It only protects a concrete `UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE` request when the city has fewer strict city defenders than `AI_minDefenders() + plot Settlers`, or when the empire is in the same minimal military-per-city state used by the immediate post-Settler defense path. `UNITAI_RESERVE` and `UNITAI_CITY_SPECIAL` requests remain eligible for the normal SAS defender-to-offense optimization. Thus the change tightens the meaning of "excess defender" rather than creating special wrappers or disabling the optimization broadly.

The final save-file 456 run confirmed the intended separation: all 264 minimum-defender choices, all 34 existing-Settler escort-defense choices, all 8 zero-defender choices and all 5 quick post-Settler defense choices kept their requested defensive UnitAI. Ordinary excess-defender conversion remained active; 15 `UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE`-to-offense substitutions still occurred, all from floating-defender production rather than the protected safety branches. Save file 457 independently reproduced the result: 262 minimum-defender completions, 24 existing-Settler escort defenses and 9 zero-defender branches had zero SAS role rewrites, while the safeguard itself fired 120 times and every protected request remained a defender. Floating-defender production still produced 65 ordinary role substitutions in that run, confirming that the original anti-overdefense optimization remains functional.

Fixed/improved with the help of ChatGPT-5.6-Sol thanks.

<a id="ki-197.5"></a>

## KI#197.5 - (Fixed/Improved) Base AdvCiv/K-Mod generic city-hunting-stack production ignored military unit-spending limits and could keep growing peaceful offensive stacks far above budget

After the floating-defender and strict-defender fixes, the remaining production logs exposed another inherited spending bypass in `CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction`. Base AdvCiv/K-Mod contains an early "city hunting stack" block intended to give the AI an appetite for offensive units on tight maps. It can request `UNITAI_ATTACK` or `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` before the later generic military-spending gate, and the inherited block has no equivalent unit-spending check. Direct comparison with Base AdvCiv 1.13 confirmed that this generic stack-building behavior is inherited.

The pre-fix save-file 456 run recorded 53 actual `start city attack stack` choices. Nine occurred at or above `max+15`; only one of those nine was during a land war, leaving eight peaceful over-budget stack starts. The clearest example was Roosevelt on turn 100: America had 3 cities, no land war and no immediate danger, but unit spending was 200 against a normal maximum of 76 (`max+15=91`), and the generic city-hunting branch still ordered another `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` Axeman. This was not a local defense invariant or a bounded target requirement; it was a generic offensive-stack heuristic continuing despite the normal military budget already being far exceeded.

AdvCiv-SAS now applies the same `max+15` military-spending headroom to the unit-building portion of this generic city-hunting block while peaceful. Land-war behavior is left unchanged, so an actual war can still override the ordinary budget. The experience-building opportunity at the start of the block is also unchanged because it is not another unit order. Importantly, the separate `advc.300` Barbarian-city attacker logic immediately below remains independent: that path estimates a concrete number of attackers from `AI_neededCityAttackersVsBarbarians()` and its existing safety margin, so it is a bounded target-specific requirement rather than the generic stack-growth loop being fixed here.

The final save-file 456 validation evaluated the city-hunting spending gate 1,976 times. 391 peaceful over-budget evaluations were blocked, while 188 over-budget land-war evaluations remained eligible. There were 44 actual generic stack starts; zero peaceful starts occurred at or above `max+15`, and the only actual over-budget start was a deliberate wartime case. The targeted Barbarian-attacker path remained available independently, including cases where the generic stack was blocked but a calculated Barbarian-city requirement still justified a unit.

Save file 457 independently confirmed the rule on a different game history: 2,122 gate evaluations included 351 peaceful over-budget cases that were blocked and 20 over-budget land-war cases that remained eligible. The run produced 45 actual generic city-hunting-stack starts and none occurred above `max+15`. The targeted Barbarian-attacker path fired only once in that run and did so below the spending threshold. Together with save file 456, this shows that the cure removes a broad peaceful offensive spending bypass without suppressing wartime stack growth or the separate bounded Barbarian-conquest logic.

Fixed/improved with the help of ChatGPT-5.6-Sol thanks.

## KI#197.6 - (Fixed SAS naval-trade accounting defect) Dual-coast ports omitted docked ships

Queue-005 WIP284 found that the corrected naval-trade cap still counted docked ships only for one selected water area. A dual-coast city's ship on the other adjacent sea could be omitted and trigger unnecessary production.

Update: the completed repair uses the same dual-coast predicate as KI#193.2 for both existing ships and sea units under construction. A ship docked or queued at a port now counts for the selected sea when either the city's primary accessible water area or `secondWaterArea()` matches it; ships physically at sea retain their direct area test.

The repaired DLL compiled successfully, and a water-rich full autoplay completed without an observed production or runtime issue.

The continued KI#197 military-production audit exposed another inherited `CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction` edge case in AdvCiv's special naval-trade sea-explorer fallback. Base AdvCiv/K-Mod deliberately handles trade exploration separately from the ordinary sea-explorer target: if a city has access to naval trade, the branch ignores `seaExplorersTarget`, counts up to three "water units" in the relevant water area, and then has a 25% chance to request `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA`. Direct comparison with Base AdvCiv 1.13 confirmed that this behavior is inherited.

Dedicated diagnostics showed two problems with the inherited eligibility test. First, `CvArea::getNumAIUnits(..., NO_UNITAI)` counts units physically located in the water area, so docked ships and ships already being trained are omitted even though they already satisfy the intended small-navy safety cap; it can also count non-sea units located on water plots. Second, despite an inherited comment saying that unrevealed tiles would be the preferable criterion, the branch had no requirement that any water actually remain unrevealed. In the pre-fix save-file 456 run, 32 naval-trade explorer choices were made. Twenty-five occurred with zero unrevealed water tiles, 22 occurred while the team already had at least three actual sea-domain ships including docked/queued ships, and 14 occurred while it already had at least ten.

The late-game examples made the effect especially clear. On turn 258, Germany had already met every surviving civilization, the entire 3,080-plot main ocean was revealed, `seaExplorerTarget=0`, and three naval units were docked; the inherited counter nevertheless saw zero units in the water area and Frankfurt produced a 200-hammer Attack Submarine as `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA`. On turn 270, Egypt likewise had zero unrevealed water, `seaExplorerTarget=0`, and 11 docked naval units while the inherited count was zero; Pi-Ramesses and Giza both ordered Attack Submarines and Akhetaten ordered a Destroyer through the same fallback.

AdvCiv-SAS keeps the special naval-trade fallback, its inherited cap of three ships, and its 25% explorer choice, but makes those prerequisites mean what the branch intended. It now counts actual `DOMAIN_SEA` units associated with the relevant water area, including ships docked in coastal cities and sea-domain UnitAIs already being trained there. The fallback also requires at least one unrevealed tile in that water area. The ordinary later target-based sea-explorer path is unchanged, and the special trade path still does not depend on `seaExplorerTarget`, so it can continue to cover a separate water area or trade-exploration need that the ordinary target does not represent.

The confirming save-file 456 rerun logged 437 naval-trade fallback evaluations. Only 44 met the corrected eligibility conditions and attempted the inherited 25% roll, producing 8 actual explorer choices. Every actual choice had unrevealed water and fewer than three corrected sea units; none occurred above the normal `max+15` military-spending allowance in this run. Three of the eight successful choices still had `seaExplorerTarget=0` (Cologne on turn 114, Munich on turn 227 and Bursa on turn 254), confirming that the distinct naval-trade fallback remains functional instead of merely duplicating the ordinary target-based explorer rule. The earlier fully explored / already-large-navy Attack Submarine and Destroyer production disappeared because those states are no longer eligible.

The original fix was implemented with the help of ChatGPT-5.6-Sol; its dual-coast omission was reopened through ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's Queue-005 WIP284 audit and completed with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.
