## KI#523 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv arithmetic defect) Weighted odds could not undo personality after clamping

AdvCiv's `AI_getWeightedOdds` intends to remove the leader's optimistic `AttackOddsChange`, apply nonlinear opportunity/value adjustments to the actual combat odds, and then restore the personality modifier. Both inherited odds producers had already added that modifier and clamped their public result to 1..99, however, so subtraction could not recover information lost at either endpoint. A true 99% chance with +16 personality became 83% before weighting, while a true rounded 0% chance with no bonus arrived as 1% and bypassed the explicit small-stack zero-odds safeguard. The nonlinear production, terrain, healing and city-opportunity adjustments made this materially different from merely adding the same bonus later.

The fix lets `CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds` optionally return pre-personality odds over the full 0..100 range. Weighted group odds request that exact value for the already selected attacker whenever the public result is at a lossy 1/99 boundary; ordinary unclamped values retain the exact and cheaper subtraction. The inherited nonlinear policy then runs before restoring `AttackOddsChange` and the public 1..99 clamp. Other odds callers retain their existing adjusted/clamped contract by default, including both LFB and legacy/air-aware calculations.

An initial combat-heavy Huge Pangaea, Normal-speed autoplay with 16 independent teams, standard Aggressive AI/full UWAI and No Events completed 418 turns and ended normally by Space Race victory. Its deliberately warlike cast was Alexander, Boudica, Cyrus, Ewuare, Genghis Khan, Gilgamesh, Grace O'Malley, Hannibal, Julius Caesar, Mao Zedong, Moctezuma, Napoleon, Ragnar, Saladin, Shaka and Stalin. Napoleon and Ragnar are the current personalities used by the audit's concrete reachable +16 `AttackOddsChange` proof.

`SASGameRecord_20260831T164003Z_new2.log` subsequently exposed that the initial run had inadvertently retained a Release DLL. After a clean Debug-opt compilation, the same turn-0 save and roster were replayed to provide a controlled comparison. `SASGameRecord_20260831T170856Z_load1.log` identifies the new DLL as Debug-opt and records all 500 turns completing normally by Time victory, with 2,967 player combat wins, 2,860 player combat losses and 4,898 units produced across its intervals. These totals come directly from its `GAME_RECORD_MILITARY_FLOW` and `GAME_RECORD_PRODUCTION_FLOW` rows rather than visual estimation; its final `GAME_RECORD_RUN_STATUS` likewise supplies the eliminations, winner, score and military-power result below. Its context fields also say `fassertEnabled=0`, so this is optimized symbol-bearing coverage rather than assertion coverage. Recording DLL build type, fingerprint and source/save context made the validation-provenance mistake visible and allowed it to be corrected instead of inferred from memory. Exact 0/99 clamp transitions remain source/arithmetic verified.

One unrelated, non-blocking AI observation from the replay is retained for future investigation: a Ragnar War Elephant visibly remained roughly 50 turns two tiles west and one tile south of a Numidian city, then departed shortly before Gilgamesh conquered that city. This behavior is not attributed to KI#523.

This arithmetic defect was introduced by AdvCiv practical 114b and remains in Base AdvCiv 1.14; AdvCiv-SAS inherited it unchanged. Found as F200 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C++ File Audit Album review; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

### Side notes about this run (based on the SASGameRecord log)

- The replay was unusually violent even for this deliberately aggressive roster: its almost six recorded player combat wins per turn are about 16% above the initial run's rate, eight of the 16 civilizations were eliminated, and Genghis Khan finished with the winning score and strongest military. In less formal terms, SASGameRecord shows that it became a useful "den of tigers" stress sample as well as controlled KI#523 validation. Its long timeline, heavy combat, eliminations, production history and explicit build/source/save metadata also make it a richer replacement for the maintained SASGameRecord example.
- The raw replacement example deliberately retains the source commit hash captured when the game ran. This documentation and example replacement were then added by amending that commit, so the recorded hash names its pre-amend object; the commit count/version remains correct because an amend replaces one commit with one commit. Rewriting generated evidence to contain the later hash would falsely imply that the amended documentation existed in the DLL's runtime source context.

Oh yes. Violent. Very violent. 😄

Not merely “Aggressive AI produced a few more wars.” This run eventually turned into something resembling a 500-turn continental meat grinder followed by a nuclear late game.

A few headline numbers from the record:

16 civilizations started; only 8 survived.
2,752 lethal civ-vs-civ battles, plus 709 nonlethal combat-limit engagements.
Another 323 lethal battles involved Barbarians, mostly early-game.
147 cities were conquered directly from one civilization by another.
23 cities were deliberately razed by civilizations, destroying 235 population at the moment of razing. Barbarians razed another 3 tiny cities.
The logger reconstructs 99 war-pair episodes. Of those, 54 were direct declarations; much of the remainder came from vassal alignment.
There was at least one active war during roughly 375 of the 501 turns, and at peak there were 9 simultaneous war pairs.
The game actually ended with 9 wars still active. 😄

And then there's the nuclear part.

The civs produced 60 nuclear weapons: 47 ICBMs + 13 tactical nukes. At turn 500, only 26 nukes remained in surviving inventories. I wouldn't equate the missing 34 mechanically with 34 successful nuclear strikes—some could have been intercepted/destroyed/otherwise consumed—but the log contains actual nuclear-fallout events beginning on turn 301 and continuing as late as turn 495, plus large MEMORY_NUKED_US counts between surviving powers.

So yes, there was an actual nuclear exchange, not merely deterrence. 😆

The diplomacy memories are particularly amusing/grim. By the end they include things like approximately:

Genghis → Boudica: 14 “nuked us” memories
Boudica → Ewuare: 7
Saladin → Moctezuma: 6
Ewuare → Boudica: 5
Genghis → Ewuare: 4

Those memory counts aren't necessarily one-to-one with individual warheads because a nuclear blast can implicate more than one party, but they're enough to establish that this was not a one-off Hiroshima moment.

The casualty leaders are fun too

For lethal civ-vs-civ combat:

| Leader           |   Kills | Losses |      Net |
| ---------------- | ------: | -----: | -------: |
| **Ewuare**       | **530** |    343 | **+187** |
| **Genghis Khan** | **484** |    475 |       +9 |
| **Ragnar**       | **309** |    198 | **+111** |
| **Cyrus**        |     259 |    322 |      -63 |
| **Saladin**      |     257 |    207 |      +50 |
| Julius Caesar    |     228 |    236 |       -8 |
| Boudica          |     205 |    224 |      -19 |

So interestingly, Genghis won the game but wasn't remotely the most efficient battlefield killer. Ewuare had the spectacular combat record: 530 kills against 343 losses.

Genghis's distinguishing characteristic was territorial appetite.

He directly conquered 40 civ-owned cities, by far the most of anyone. Ragnar took 19; Ewuare and Julius took 17 each; Saladin 15.

And Genghis directly declared war 10 times, also the highest total, followed by Julius with 9 and Saladin with 7.

So Genghis winning a Time Victory with the highest score (4947) and highest power (8699) feels appropriate: he didn't quite conquer the world, but he spent much of history trying. 😄

There were actually two major killing seasons

Breaking civ-vs-civ lethal battles into 50-turn blocks gives the texture:

| Turns       | Lethal battles | City conquests |
| ----------- | -------------: | -------------: |
| 100–149     |             93 |              9 |
| 150–199     |            245 |             17 |
| **200–249** |        **586** |         **28** |
| **250–299** |        **547** |         **25** |
| 300–349     |            309 |             17 |
| 350–399     |            138 |              7 |
| **400–449** |        **548** |         **25** |
| 450–499     |            271 |             17 |

So there was an enormous turn 200–300 world-war period, relative cooling around 350–400, and then another gigantic explosion after 400.

That second phase is especially nasty because it's occurring in the robotic-infantry / levitation-artillery / tactical-nuke era.

By turns 491–500 alone, Boudica lost 39 units in ten turns while winning only 10 battles. Genghis won 37 and lost 17. And despite the clock literally about to end the game, the major powers were still building robotic infantry, levitation artillery, tactical nukes and ICBMs.

Nobody got the memo that it was turn 500. 😂

And cities changed hands constantly

There were 164 city ownership changes overall. Six were peaceful trades; 158 were conquests, including some Barbarian interactions.

Some cities became genuine footballs. Bulawayo, for example, appears changing hands repeatedly among Zulu/Persia/Ragnar/Rome/Genghis-era ownership chains. Ergili flips from Genghis to Gilgamesh on turn 472 and straight back to Genghis on turn 473.

The late game is particularly savage. Between turn 478 and 499 you have cities such as Urhonigbe, Durnovaria, Gwato, Ugo, Texcoco, Camulodunum, Bibracte, Vienne, Gergovia and Verlamion being captured, and several are immediately or subsequently razed.

And these aren't little size-2 ancient settlements anymore. Late razes include:

Gergovia population 16
Verlamion population 17
Gwato population 13
Durnovaria population 13

So the late game wasn't symbolic warfare. Whole mature industrial/future-era cities were disappearing.

My violence rating

For a Huge Pangaea, 16 civ, Aggressive AI, UWAI FULL, 500-turn game:

9/10 violence.

I reserve 10/10 for something like nearly universal extermination/conquest victory plus sustained nuclear apocalypse.

This one weirdly retained enough geopolitical balance that eight civilizations were still alive and the game reached a Time Victory. That's actually what makes it more interesting: it wasn't one unstoppable conqueror rolling the map.

It was a multipolar, self-renewing war system.

Civilizations got powerful enough to fight huge wars, weaken one another, recover, realign through vassalage, and then do it again—until they eventually started throwing nuclear weapons around.

So perhaps:

Not “everyone died.”

More:

“Half the world died, the surviving half fought thousands of battles over 147 captured cities, then invented ICBMs and continued fighting until the calendar forcibly ended the game.”

Yeah. Violent run. xD

Recounted with the help of ChatGPT-5.6-Sol (temporary chat), with some earlier bits from GPT-5.6-Sol (i.e. on Codex) thanks.

## KI#524 - (Fixed AdvCiv-SAS KI#319 regression) Non-head bombard detachment was mistaken for no progress

Screenshots/files for this issue: same google drive folder link as KI#524.6.

AdvCiv's `AI_bombardCity` selects one bombard unit independently of the group head, detaches an `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` unit into its own group, executes Bombard there and returns so the surviving original group can be evaluated again. When the selected unit was not the original head, SAS's KI#319 tripwire could see the same head identity, role, position, movement and empty mission queue in the original group and force it to skip despite its membership having decreased through a successful action.

The repair snapshots group size and requires membership count to remain unchanged before applying `MISSION_SKIP`. This complements KI#522 rather than replacing it: cargo can change without membership change, while a non-head bombard split changes membership without changing cargo or the existing head. AdvCiv `advc.004c` introduced the deliberate bombard detachment and Base AdvCiv naturally re-evaluates the surviving group; the conflicting no-progress safeguard is SAS custom logic, making this an AdvCiv-SAS regression. Found as F201/provisional KI#524 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C018-WIP04 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

<a id="ki-524.2"></a>

## KI#524.2 - (Fixed inherited BtS/K-Mod/AdvCiv crash) Spy-border verification dereferenced an unplaced unit

Screenshots/files for this issue: same google drive folder link as KI#524.6.

During a Huge Continents Debug-opt autoplay, turn 430 crashed in `CvTeam::verifySpyUnitsValidPlot` while a player's turn-start espionage points were being applied. The matching PDB resolved the invalid read to `pUnit->getPlot().getOwner()`. `SASGameRecord_20260827T173601Z_new1.log` supplied the missing gameplay sequence around that source line: its final turn-430 records show several unit deaths followed by Essen being acquired and razed immediately before the crash. This initially narrowed the trigger to the city-capture/raze sequence rather than an arbitrary corrupted map plot or ordinary Spy movement; the later Python exception and KI#524.6 investigation proved that the object was a reset/unplaced unit-container entry left by the inherited Partisans `initUnit(NO_UNIT)` failure. The helper nevertheless read every unit's plot before testing whether the unit was a Spy, although only Spies are relevant to its border-validity work.

The repair checks for a non-null plot before reading either unit-info-backed Spy state or plot ownership, filters out non-Spies next, then preserves the existing border-access test and delayed relocation. This order matters: an initial repair checked `isSpy()` before `plot()`, and the same autosave still crashed at `isSpy()` because the malformed reset object was not safe for that access either. This addresses the helper's actual placed-Spy input contract rather than special-casing the observed battle, city, player or turn. The unsafe ordering exists in Firaxis BtS, K-Mod 1.46 and Base AdvCiv 1.14; AdvCiv changed the pointer expression to its reference accessor but retained the same unconditional dereference. This is therefore an inherited BtS crash rather than an AdvCiv-SAS regression or a consequence of KI#521, KI#522 or KI#524.

The crash was diagnosed from `crash_t430_pdb.txt` with the retained matching Debug-opt intermediates and correlated with the named SASGameRecord above. The first repaired replay produced `crash_t430_pdb_after_fix_still.txt`, moving the fault from null-plot dereference to `isSpy()` and thereby establishing the required guard order. The PDBs identified which accesses failed; the game record explained what had happened immediately beforehand, allowing the repair to follow the helper's real placed-Spy scope. Replaying `AutoSave_AD-2068.CivBeyondSwordSave`, the latest pre-crash autosave retained from the run, remains the direct repair test. Investigated, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#524.3 - (Fixed AdvCiv-SAS WAR diagnostic crash) Military-posture logging inspected an unplaced unit

Screenshots/files for this issue: same google drive folder link as KI#524.6.

After the reordered KI#524.2 guard passed its former crash site, the same deterministic `AutoSave_AD-2068.CivBeyondSwordSave` replay advanced farther into turn 430 and crashed in `getSASBBAITeamMilitaryPosture`. `crasht_t430_pdb_still_crash2.txt` resolved the new invalid read to the helper's combat classification. The helper obtained the unit's nullable plot, then called `canDefend`, `baseCombatStr` and `airBaseCombatStr` before checking that plot; the malformed Partisans object later proved by KI#524.6 therefore reached unsafe unit-info-backed access through SAS's WAR level-2 logging path.

The repair rejects an unplaced unit immediately after reading its nullable plot, before combat classification. This is also the correct diagnostic meaning: an unplaced object is not part of the team's deployable military posture and should not increase its military total while contributing to no territory category. This helper was introduced by AdvCiv-SAS WAR diagnostics and has no counterpart in BtS, K-Mod or Base AdvCiv, so KI#524.3 is an AdvCiv-SAS diagnostic regression sharing KI#524.2's empirical trigger rather than another inherited crash.

The original SASGameRecord remains valuable across both defects: its unit deaths and Essen capture/raze immediately before the failures identify the shared Partisans-trigger window, while the successive matching PDBs distinguish the inherited Spy verifier from this later SAS logging consumer. ## KI#524.4 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv AI-upgrade crash) Post-turn upgrade candidates included an unplaced unit

Screenshots/files for this issue: same google drive folder link as KI#524.6.

After the KI#524.2 and KI#524.3 guards both passed their former crash sites, the same deterministic `AutoSave_AD-2068.CivBeyondSwordSave` replay advanced farther into turn 430 and crashed during `CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnUnitsPost`. The matching Debug-opt PDB in `crash_t430_pdb_still_crashes_3.txt` resolved the invalid read to `AI_unitImpassables`, called with `NO_UNIT` by the first post-turn upgrade pass. AdvCiv's `advc.131e` code copied every object in the player's unit container into an experience-sorted upgrade vector; the malformed Partisans object later proved by KI#524.6 therefore survived the sort until the impassable pass read its invalid unit type.

The repair excludes unplaced units while constructing the cached upgrade vector, before sorting or any unit-info-backed upgrade checks. This follows the operation's real contract rather than teaching `AI_unitImpassables` to accept an invalid unit type: every legitimate upgrade candidate is placed, and later passes already unconditionally inspect its plot, city, danger and group state. BtS and K-Mod also assume that the post-turn upgrade loop receives placed units, but the cached pointer vector and exact failing path are inherited from AdvCiv `advc.131e` and remain in Base AdvCiv 1.14. KI#524.4 is therefore an inherited AdvCiv crash, not an AdvCiv-SAS regression.

The same SASGameRecord remains useful evidence for the shared Partisans-trigger window, while this third PDB distinguishes the AdvCiv upgrade consumer from the earlier inherited Spy verifier and SAS WAR diagnostic helper. ## KI#525 - (Fixed AdvCiv-SAS KI#319 regression) Consumed queued group attack was mistaken for no progress

K-Mod can retain a queued group-attack retry while another combat occupies the source or destination plot. If that combat removes the final defender, the waiting unit automatically advances and can retain movement, while the queued retry flag survives. On the group's next update, SAS's KI#319 no-progress guard snapshots the ordinary head/group fields, consumes the now-stale queued attack, and sees the retry fail because the group already occupies its old target. Clearing the queued-attack state is legitimate progress, but the incomplete signature treated it as a stuck iteration and issued `MISSION_SKIP` instead of letting the still-movable group reassess.

The fix snapshots `AI_isGroupAttack()` with the other progress dimensions and permits the fallback only when that state is unchanged too. The inherited queued-combat retry and automatic movement remain unchanged; only SAS's later false no-progress classification is corrected.

This is an AdvCiv-SAS KI#319 progress-signature regression exposed by inherited K-Mod queued-combat lifecycle, not an original BtS, K-Mod or AdvCiv defect. ## KI#526 - (Fixed AdvCiv-SAS KI#319 regression) Non-head immediate movement was mistaken for no progress

K-Mod deliberately lets an AI group reconsider after a synchronous Pillage when all members can still move. A mixed group can select a faster non-head unit to pillage, spend only that unit's movement and return with its temporary mission already removed. The route or improvement and non-head movement changed, but SAS's KI#319 signature observed only the head's movement; with membership, cargo, queue and head state otherwise unchanged, it incorrectly issued `MISSION_SKIP` and suppressed K-Mod's intended same-turn reassessment.

The fix snapshots the sum of every current group member's remaining movement and requires that aggregate to remain unchanged before applying the fallback. The existing membership check keeps this aggregate comparison unambiguous when units join or leave, while any member spending movement now counts as real progress.

## KI#528 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv ordering defect) Undefended-city Bombard priorities collapsed to zero

AdvCiv's smart ordering for a human group Bombard derives a distinct priority for each eligible siege unit, then attenuates that priority by the unit's attack odds against the city. A legal undefended-city Bombard reports conventional 100% attack odds, so multiplying by `1 - odds` reduced every otherwise distinct priority to zero. The first eligible unit in group-list order therefore spent its action even when the promotion, bombard-damage and waste calculations preferred another unit.

The fix applies defender-odds attenuation only when the target has a real defender. Undefended targets retain all other smart-order factors, including current hit points when the city is considered easy to capture, intended promotion use, bombard damage, wasted damage, movement and collateral value. This remains distinct from KI#521's already-fixed false Debug assertion for the same legal target state.

After compilation, a fresh Balanced Huge game with 16 independent teams completed a full autoplay and ended through Space Race victory on turn 492 without an observed issue. The precise human group-Bombard ordering state remains source-verified rather than manually constructed.

This is an inherited AdvCiv practical-2809 ordering defect, not an AdvCiv-SAS change. Found as F205 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C++ File Audit Album review; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

Inherited assault declaration intent and SAS's opportunistic launch both require that capability, while `AI_enemyTargetMissions` counts only attack-capable cargo as strategic pressure for assault groups. ## KI#530 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv Bombard defect) Peaceful foreign units counted as attackers

AdvCiv's smart human Bombard ordering estimates whether the city is easy to capture by scanning every unit on the bombarder's plot and accepting any non-bombarder that can move or attack into the target. That generic entry predicate admitted peaceful foreign units through Open Borders and admitted same-owner noncombat infiltrators such as Spies through ordinary movement. Neither can perform the immediate assault whose strength this census is intended to estimate, so unrelated units could change which siege unit spent its action.

The fix counts only units owned by the human group owner that can move now and can enter the target specifically as an attack. It therefore follows immediate assault capability rather than generic destination entry, while leaving the separate stack-strength and Bombard-priority calculations unchanged.

Update: A repair-side audit found that attack-only entry excludes every legal city-capturer when the target has no defender. KI#1040 now retains attack entry for defended targets but uses immediate capture entry for undefended cities; ownership, current movement, combat capability and no-capture restrictions remain enforced.

## KI#531 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv Bombard defect) Loaded cargo counted as city defenders

The same smart human Bombard path counted all enemy units that can defend, including combat-capable units loaded as cargo. Actual primary-defender selection explicitly excludes loaded cargo. The fix retains the inherited enemy/can-defend predicate but excludes loaded cargo from this city-defender census, matching the relevant primary-defender contract. This deliberately does not remove cargo from collateral-damage estimation: loaded combat cargo can be selected as a collateral victim, which is a different runtime population.

## KI#534 - (Fixed inherited K-Mod/AdvCiv debug-assertion defect) Planned-war census inspected transient empty groups

The census followed the empty group's stale MissionAI plot into `AI_isDeclareWar`, whose inherited leading assertion requires a head unit even though its later release guard safely returns false when the head is null.

The repair skips zero-unit groups before reading their mission target or war intent. This does not change a valid mission count: an empty group contains no units or cargo and cannot contribute to this census. BtS contains the contradictory assertion and null-safe release guard; K-Mod combines it with the BBAI target-mission census, supported empty-group lifecycle and pre-war caller, while AdvCiv retains that interaction. KI#534 is therefore inherited from K-Mod/AdvCiv rather than introduced by AdvCiv-SAS. ## KI#535 - (Fixed inherited K-Mod regression) Force update could cancel a newer amphibious group attack

K-Mod practical 428 protected deferred amphibious group attacks because a loaded sea transport can order its lower-priority land cargo to attack before the cargo group's own turn. Practical 846 later changed force update into a turn-start request that every AI group receive at least one update, but left two consumers where that old marker overruled a group attack queued later in the same movement phase. The player update's separation pre-pass could split the group, or `CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update` could cancel its continuation before executing it. An AI naval invasion could consequently stop after its first cargo-unit attack instead of following through with the remaining attackers.

The repair relies on the exact state provenance rather than a broad scheduler change. `CvSelectionGroup::doTurn` is the sole live producer of `setForceUpdate(true)`, and it already clears the mission queue and cancels every pre-existing group attack. Therefore, when force update and a queued group attack coexist, the attack is newer state and must take precedence. The separation pre-pass now retains K-Mod's protection for a group in the midst of attacking, regardless of the stale marker, and `AI_update` lets its existing loop consume the queued continuation while clearing force update normally. The update-at-least-once purpose of K-Mod 846 remains intact, as does ordinary force separation when no group attack is queued.

After a clean Debug-opt compilation, a Huge Archipelago game using Tiny Islands, Normal speed, 16 independent teams, standard Aggressive AI/full UWAI and No Events completed normally through Space Race victory on turn 404. `SASGameRecord_20260831T173535Z_new1.log` confirms the Debug-opt DLL fingerprint, naval-heavy map classification and completed autoplay, and records multiple surviving `UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA` groups and transport fleets. This provides broad runtime coverage of the relevant naval-AI environment; the exact force-update plus newly queued multi-unit amphibious continuation remains source/lifecycle verified because that transient internal state is not logged directly.

This is an inherited K-Mod regression: practical 428 introduced the intended amphibious continuation protection, practical 846 partially undermined it, and final K-Mod 1.46, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and AdvCiv-SAS retained that interaction. The exact transport-before-cargo ordering and both stale-marker consumers were source-verified. ## KI#536 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI cache-reset defect) New games and loaded saves could retain stale human-capitulation authorization

`UWAICache::m_readyToCapitulateTo` is serialized temporal state authorizing capitulation to particular human teams. `init`, `uninit` and save loading all reuse the same player-owned cache object and call its full `clear(false)`, but that reset erased the neighboring persistent state without clearing this set. Reading a save consequently produced the union of the previous in-memory set and the saved set; starting a new game in the same Civ4 process could likewise inherit authorization from the previous game occupying that player slot. Ordinary surrender requirements still applied, but the explicit current-war decision gate could be satisfied by stale state.

The repair clears `m_readyToCapitulateTo` only inside the full-reset branch. It deliberately preserves the set during the ordinary per-turn `clear(true)` cache refresh, because that authorization must survive routine recomputation until its separate diplomacy lifecycle changes it. The omission dates to AdvCiv's initial 2017 WarAndPeace/UWAI cache integration and remains in Base AdvCiv 1.14; AdvCiv-SAS inherited it unchanged. A current-build BTG Lagoon autoplay was saved at turn 201, reloaded without restarting Civ4 and completed successfully, exercising cache reconstruction and continued play. Creating the exact stale authorization in a preceding game was not forced, so removal of that specific state remains source/lifecycle verified. Found as F213/provisional KI#536 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 `UWAICache.cpp` audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#537 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI military-cache defect) Losing every trainable branch candidate retained obsolete production capacity

Every regular UWAI cache refresh asks each persistent `MilitaryBranch` to recompute its typical currently trainable unit. The base refresh and the independent `NuclearArsenal` override only overwrote their stored unit and power after finding a candidate; when no candidate survived, they retained the previous turn's values. Current SAS can reproduce this for nuclear production after the owner loses its last connected Uranium, while losing a qualifying coastal city or another removable prerequisite can affect other branches. UWAI could therefore reserve forecast production for military capacity that the player could no longer build. Fleet also retained the former typical ship's bombard flag after correctly transitioning to no candidate.

The repair begins both refresh implementations from `NO_UNIT` and zero typical power, before the nuclear no-capital return, so the cache can represent the valid candidate-to-none transition. Fleet now recomputes bombard capability to false when no typical ship exists. Existing-unit counts and total military power remain untouched because they describe the units actually possessed, not future trainability. This refresh omission and the contradictory forecast safeguard date to AdvCiv's initial 2017 WarAndPeace/UWAI integration and remain in Base AdvCiv 1.14; AdvCiv-SAS inherited them unchanged. The successful full autoplay and BTG Lagoon save/reload continuation provide practical regression coverage; deliberately gaining and then removing the last valid branch candidate was not forced, so that exact transition remains source-verified. Found as F214/provisional KI#537 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#538 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI leader-migration defect) A promoted leader inherited stale or default-true war hireability

UWAI stores team-level `CanBeHiredAgainst` state inside the current team leader's player cache. A non-leader's private map is not kept synchronized while another player leads and its declared default is true. When team leadership changed through leader death or a Permanent Alliance, `onTeamLeaderChanged` copied other leader-owned state but did not initialize this map, despite its own comment requiring the new leader to start false. The promoted player's stale or default-true private values consequently became authoritative and could prematurely admit sponsored-war evaluation for a human sponsor in a large game.

The repair explicitly fills the promoted leader's hireability map with false, allowing normal UWAI war planning to recompute it afterward. It does not copy the former leader's personality/planning-derived bits and does not bypass any ordinary war-legality, attitude or power checks. The leader-migration callback predates the hireability cache; AdvCiv practical 1343 added the cache and its live trade gate without extending that callback, and practical 2920 later documented the intended false initialization without implementing it. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the omission, so KI#538 is an inherited AdvCiv UWAI migration defect rather than an AdvCiv-SAS regression.

## KI#539 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI AgentIterator regression) Permanent Alliance absorption doubled the absorbed leader's own war history

The original UWAI Permanent Alliance merge applied the absorbed leader's persistent history to the surviving team's pre-merge member list. AdvCiv practical 1818 replaced that cached membership with a live `MemberAIIter`, but `CvTeam::addTeam` invoked the merge only after reassigning every absorbed player to the surviving team. The iterator therefore traversed both original sides. In particular, the absorbed leader added its own cache to itself, deterministically doubling every nonzero past-war score; other absorbed members also received history outside the original recipient contract.

The same refactor-era implementation iterated only currently alive major target teams while copying persistent history. An eliminated rival's history could therefore be omitted during the alliance and become relevant again if that rival was revived. The altered or missing scores feed learned military confidence and invasion forecasts.

The repair performs the existing UWAI member-cache merge immediately before player reassignment, while live membership still identifies only the original surviving side, and copies every civilization-team key rather than narrowing persistent history to targets alive at that moment. The absorbed leader remains accessible through its saved player ID, and the later KI#551 outsider target-key migration remains separate after the core team merge. This restores the exact recipient and target domains rather than special-casing only the self-add iteration. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the regression, making KI#539 inherited from the AdvCiv AgentIterator refactor rather than AdvCiv-SAS.

The same `SASGameRecord_20260828T094941Z_new1.log` confirms the successful post-refinement mixed-team Permanent-Alliances-enabled run; no new Permanent Alliance formed, so the exact merge remains source/lifecycle verified. ## KI#540 - (Fixed AdvCiv-SAS cross-layer regression) UWAI mistook Jungle for Fallout and enabled cleanup at Metal Casting

`UWAICache::updateCanScrub` inferred Fallout by selecting the first feature with at most -50 health, then looked for a known build technology that removed that feature. Base BtS/AdvCiv data made Fallout the only matching feature, but SAS increased Jungle to -50 health and it precedes Fallout in XML/enum order. The cached `eFallout` was therefore actually Jungle: learning Metal Casting, the Jungle-removal technology, made UWAI report Fallout cleanup available many eras before Environmentalism. Nuclear-war valuation consequently understated expected population and asset losses even though Worker legality itself remained correct.

The repair caches the exact `FEATURE_FALLOUT` type and preserves the broader intended question of whether any currently known build can remove it. Feature identity no longer depends on health balance or XML order. The brittle heuristic dates to AdvCiv's initial 2017 WarAndPeace/UWAI integration, but Base AdvCiv 1.14 still satisfies its old data assumption; SAS feature-health changes made the defect gameplay-live, so KI#540 is an AdvCiv-SAS cross-layer regression rather than a live base-data bug. ## KI#541 - (Fixed AdvCiv-SAS cross-layer regression) Player-level transport eligibility ignored city resources and placement

`UWAICache::updateTransports` used `CvPlayer::canTrain` to answer whether the owner could train any assault transport. That player-level check covers civilization mapping, technologies and global limits but not city plot-group resources or sea-unit placement. SAS makes Galley obsolete at Astronomy and Galleon obsolete at Combustion, leaving the Oil-requiring Transport as the only assault-sea candidate afterward. An Oil-less post-Combustion civilization therefore passed the player check even though no city could train any transport, falsely enabling deep-sea reachability and defeating SAS's no-lift war-target gate.

The repair retains the cheap player-level prefilter but additionally requires at least one actual owned city whose `CvCity::canTrain` accepts the unit before setting either cached transport capability. This captures connected resources, coastal placement, replacements and other local prerequisites without inventing partial Oil-specific logic. Existing already-built transports remain outside this explicitly trainability-based contract.

The coarse player-level assumption dates to AdvCiv's initial UWAI cache, but Base AdvCiv's non-obsolete resource-free Galleon masks this exact all-candidates-untrainable state; SAS's deliberate obsolescence chain activates it, making KI#541 an AdvCiv-SAS cross-layer regression. The huge BTG Cross autoplay completed successfully; an Oil-less post-Combustion empire with no city-trainable transport was not deliberately forced, so that exact capability transition remains source-verified. Found as F218/provisional KI#541 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#542 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI logic bug) Cumulative peaceful-victory stage checks made stage 4 unreachable

`UWAICache::goldPerProdVictory` tested Culture/Space stage 3 before stage 4 for both the owner and rivals. Victory-stage hashes deliberately retain lower-stage bits, so every stage-4 state also satisfies the stage-3 predicate and both stage-4 branches were unreachable. The resulting classifications could undervalue an owner's urgent peaceful-victory production or fail to recognize that a rival was strictly closer, feeding incorrect production opportunity costs into UWAI war evaluation whenever this term controlled the final gold-per-production estimate.

The repair queries stage 4 before stage 3 on both sides; cumulative stage construction remains unchanged. The reversed tests date to AdvCiv's initial 2017 WarAndPeace/UWAI cache and remain in Base AdvCiv 1.14, so KI#542 is inherited rather than introduced by AdvCiv-SAS. The huge BTG Cross autoplay completed successfully; no specific stage-4 owner/rival combination was forced, so the corrected classification remains source-verified. Found as F219/provisional KI#542 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#543 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI team-scope defect) Nuclear deterrence ignored teammate and master-side nuclear units

`UWAICache::teamThreat` models the long-term threat of a future war against the cache owner's team. Its rival attitude, victory pressure, alternative targets and both sides' long-term power are team-level; defensive owner power deliberately uses the owner's full master side. The inherited nuclear-deterrence term alone checked `GET_PLAYER(m_eOwner).getNumNukeUnits()`. On a normal shared team, one member with no nuclear units therefore calculated a greater threat than a teammate with nuclear units even though any declaration would start the same indivisible team war and expose the rival to the same retaliation. The same mismatch applied when the owner's master side contained the nuclear capability.

The repair queries `CvTeam::getNumNukeUnits` on the owner's master team, matching the scope already used for long-term defensive power. That API includes the team's members and vassals; it changes only the existing -0.2 deterrence term and leaves rival reachability, power and attitude logic untouched. The player-only test dates to AdvCiv's initial 2017 WarAndPeace/UWAI implementation and remains in Base AdvCiv 1.14, so KI#543 is inherited rather than introduced by AdvCiv-SAS. A full Huge Pangaea autoplay completed successfully; a teammate/master-side-only nuclear inventory was not forced, so the exact deterrence scope remains source-verified. Found as F220/provisional KI#543 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#544 - (Fixed inherited K-Mod/AdvCiv mission-census defect) Boarded cargo counted through both transport and cargo groups

K-Mod deliberately keeps loaded land units in their own `ACTIVITY_BOARDED` selection groups, and those groups remain enumerable while following the transport's plot. Both `CvPlayerAI::AI_enemyTargetMissions` and AdvCiv's overlapping `UWAICache::updateTargetMissionCount` counted every group's own units plus its cargo. A transport carrying two land units on an enemy-owned plot consequently contributed 3 through the transport group and the same 2 cargo units again through their boarded groups: 5 missions for 3 physical units. UWAI's invasion targeting begins with a threshold of 3, so that ordinary example could falsely create a mission-selected target rather than merely skewing an unused statistic.

The repair preserves the transport group's mission/destination context by counting its carried cargo, but counts only non-cargo members through each group's own unit list. Every physical unit therefore contributes at most once, including in mixed groups, and both intentionally overlapping censuses retain matching semantics. The defect combines BBAI's ancestral census with K-Mod's later persistent boarded-group representation and is inherited by AdvCiv/SAS; both K-Mod 1.46 and Base AdvCiv 1.14 retain it. A full Huge Pangaea autoplay completed successfully; the exact loaded-transport target census was not exposed directly, so its corrected multiplicity remains source-verified. Found as F221/provisional KI#544 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

As a separate side observation from that validation run, the random civilization selection chose Ireland again and Dublin initially developed slowly. `SASGameRecord_20260828T045853Z_new1.log` in save file 566 showed that Dublin's initial BFC contained 7 Forest and 1 Jungle plots, Ireland had only one Worker through turn 50, and it researched Pottery on turn 39, Agriculture on turn 48, Masonry on turn 75 and Metal Casting on turn 86. Improved city plots nevertheless rose from 1 at turns 20-40 to 6 at turn 70, 13 at turn 90 and 19 at turn 100; by turn 90 its Workers were actively removing both Forest and Jungle.

As with the earlier Spain observation under KI#547, this was feature-heavy geography plus delayed AdvCiv-SAS removal technologies, not a regression from KI#543-KI#544. Removing Pottery as an Agriculture prerequisite would be a separate global tech-tree choice and would not address this bottleneck; a future targeted refinement of the existing feature-removal technology valuation could help capitals that have unusually few usable Worker plots, especially on Rainforest or Arboria.

## KI#545 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI ScaledNum regression) Settler adjustment divided fixed expansion-site weights by 10

The original `goldPerProdSites` model weighted the five best expansion opportunities by `1.0`, `0.8`, `0.6`, `0.4` and `0.2`, then added `settlers / 10` because using current Settlers could make more remote sites more attractive. AdvCiv practical 2920 converted the formula from double to `ScaledNum` but changed `siteWeight + settlers / 10` into `(siteWeight + settlers) / 10`. With no Settlers, the best site's coefficient consequently fell from `1.0` to `0.1`; the error systematically made peaceful expansion opportunity look much cheaper when UWAI valued the production cost of war.

The repair restores the original algebra explicitly as `arSiteWeights[i] + scaled(iSettlers, 10)` while preserving all site weights, the Settler-based starting index, Barbarian-city contribution and final cap. Practical 2920 introduced this regression and Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it unchanged, so KI#545 is inherited rather than introduced by AdvCiv-SAS. A full Peirce SAS24 autoplay completed successfully, providing broad expansion and UWAI regression coverage; the exact internal site-value term remains source/arithmetic verified. Found as F222/provisional KI#545 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

<a id="ki-546"></a>

## KI#546 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI ScaledNum regression) War-trade hireability persistence lost its 1.0 probability baseline

UWAI caches whether a team remains willing to be hired into war so the human-facing war-trade availability does not flicker between reviews. The original persistence branch used `1 - (threshold - utility) / 100.0`: at the threshold an already-hireable target remained so with 100% probability, declining gradually below it. AdvCiv practical 2920's `ScaledNum` rewrite changed this to `scaled(1 - (threshold - utility), 100)`, meaning `(1 - delta) / 100`. At the threshold persistence collapsed from 100% to 1%, and ten points below it changed from 90% to a non-positive probability that always cleared the flag.

The repair restores `1 - scaled(threshold - utility, 100)`, preserving the original 1.0 baseline while leaving the FALSE-to-TRUE probability, 58% cap, utility threshold and update cadence unchanged. Practical 2920 introduced this regression and Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it unchanged, so KI#546 is inherited rather than introduced by AdvCiv-SAS. The full Peirce SAS24 autoplay completed successfully; no exact already-hireable threshold state was inspected, so the corrected persistence probabilities remain source/arithmetic verified. Found as F223/provisional KI#546 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#547 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI cache-coherency defect) Mid-turn city ownership changes left total assets at the previous city set

Screenshots/files for this issue: [google drive folder link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14xGl6mzZ8g6uSNv6FX_OC-rHHmDyWCTd?usp=sharing).

UWAI's ordinary turn refresh rebuilds its detailed city cache and then derives `m_rTotalAssets` from the cache owner's current cities. Special city-created and city-destroyed callbacks deliberately update the city set immediately during a human turn so conquests can affect fresh war and peace evaluation before the AI's next turn. Those callbacks did not recompute the aggregate: after conquest the victim's total still included the lost city and the conqueror's total still excluded it, while the detailed city set already represented the new ownership. Risk, asset-greed, nuclear-loss and other war-utility ratios could therefore combine incompatible snapshots.

The repair recomputes total assets only when the changed city belongs to the cache owner, after the city list has been added/removed and restored to its required order. Other observers avoid unnecessary aggregate work because their own holdings did not change. The omission predates AdvCiv-SAS: AdvCiv practical 1289 introduced mid-turn ownership updates without refreshing total assets, and practical 2605 retained it when splitting the modern destruction/creation callbacks. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains the defect. A full Huge Pangaea autoplay completed successfully after the repair; the immediate internal aggregate remains source/lifecycle verified.

That run also initially appeared to show unusually slow early tile development for autoplay-controlled Spain. `SASGameRecord_20260828T043216Z_new1.log` in save file 565 confirmed the outlier but explained it without a code regression: Madrid began with 12 Forest plots, Spain still had only 1 improved land plot at turns 30 and 40, and it acquired Masonry only on turn 52. AdvCiv-SAS requires Masonry to remove Forest and Metal Casting, acquired by Spain on turn 66, to remove Jungle; Bronze Working is not a feature-removal prerequisite here. Spain's development then rose from 2 improved land plots at turn 50 to 4 at turn 60 and 7 at turn 70. Its Worker had already completed a Pig Pasture and several Roads, so this was forest-heavy geography plus delayed improvement technologies rather than Worker inactivity or a consequence of the recent exact-Fallout feature fix.

Found as F224/provisional KI#547 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#548 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI revival-cache defect) Existing units were absent from the rebuilt military inventory

Screenshots/files for this issue: same google drive folder link as KI#475.3.

KI#475.3 fixed the reproducible crash caused by a player who was dead when a save loaded retaining an uninitialized UWAI cache after WorldBuilder gave that player a unit. The deeper lifecycle still lost the unit that caused revival. `CvUnit::finalizeInit` reports the new unit while its owner is dead; `CvPlayer::verifyAlive` notices that existing unit afterward and revives the owner. Death had cleared the player's incremental military counts and branches, while KI#475.3's required revival initialization creates a fresh cache with zero military. The earlier creation report is therefore discarded before `processNewPlayerInGame` immediately updates UWAI consumers. The revived civilization physically owned its Robotic Tank but UWAI modeled zero current Army power and zero non-naval units; destroying that unrecorded unit later could decrement both inventories below zero.

The repair reconstructs this exceptional inventory immediately after revival initialization and before `processNewPlayerInGame`: it scans the revived player's current units once and replays the normal unit-created accounting into the newly empty military branches and non-naval count. Ordinary per-turn cache updates remain incremental and do not gain a full unit scan. This is the logical reconstruction half of the same reproduction that exposed KI#475.3, but the omission predates AdvCiv-SAS: AdvCiv practical 2010 introduced revival processing after acknowledging that elimination deletes UWAI data, without rebuilding units that already existed before revival. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains that incomplete lifecycle.

The rebuilt Debug-opt DLL repeated the direct save-file 547 reproduction successfully. WorldBuilder gave the dead human PC a Robotic Tank, Robotic Infantry and Trireme in unowned territory, reviving that player with both land and naval military units already present; Peter received a Spearman and a Transport, with the Transport placed in Gilgamesh's territory. Exiting WorldBuilder completed without an assertion or crash. This directly exercised revival initialization and reconstruction across several military branches; combat against the active player was unnecessary because KI#548 concerns the revived owner's inventory before later consumers or destruction. Found as F225/provisional KI#548 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol and compile/runtime-tested with the help of wonderingabout, thanks.

## KI#549 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI reachability defect) A shorter secondary-area land path could hide a valid naval route

`UWAICache::City::updateDistance` separately decides whether a foreign city is strategically reachable and estimates the fastest deployment duration from each productive source city. A land path from any source may contribute its duration, but deliberately establishes global land reachability only when that source belongs to one of the AI's primary areas. A secondary colony can instead establish naval reachability. The inherited implementation accidentally coupled that existence decision to route speed: it skipped naval pathfinding when the existing land duration was already short, and even after finding water set `bReachBySea` only when the sea duration beat the land duration.

A cache owner with two substantial cities in a secondary area could therefore have both a short local land path and a valid but slower naval route to an enemy city on that landmass. The local route was intentionally insufficient to set `m_bReachByLand`, while its short duration prevented the valid water route from setting `bReachBySea`; the final gate consequently left the target at distance `-1` and removed it from UWAI's reachable-city and invasion-target sets. This was not the intended primary-area restriction: the same secondary port already established reachability whenever its naval route happened to be faster.

The repair tracks whether each source's land route qualifies for strategic land reachability. Only a qualifying short land route may retain the existing optimization that skips a naval comparison; otherwise a coastal source with cargo capability still checks whether a water route exists. Finding one now sets sea reachability independently, while the pairwise duration changes only if the sea route is actually faster. Secondary-area land paths remain unable to establish `m_bReachByLand`, and their shorter duration can still contribute once a permitted sea route proves the target strategically reachable. The mismatch dates to AdvCiv's initial 2017 WarAndPeace/UWAI implementation; practical 2767 reduced its incidence by broadening qualifying land sources to all primary areas, while practical 2929 added the speed shortcut that supplied a second skip path.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both parts, so KI#549 is inherited rather than introduced by AdvCiv-SAS. The rebuilt DLL completed a full autoplay successfully; the exact secondary-colony state with a shorter non-qualifying land path and slower valid sea route remains source-verified. Found as F226/provisional KI#549 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol and compile/runtime-tested with the help of wonderingabout, thanks.

## KI#550 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI lifecycle regression) Pure city destruction left the stateful attack-priority order stale

Screenshots/files for this issue: same as KI#547.

`sortCitiesByAttackPriority` is a greedy area-clustering pass: each candidate's priority depends partly on the area of the city selected immediately before it. Erasing an entry therefore does not generally preserve the order that a fresh sort would produce. AdvCiv practical 2605 moved the old ownership-change callback's final sort into `reportCityCreated`; ordinary capture still receives that creation half, but razing or otherwise destroying a city has no replacement callback and left the surviving target order stale during the rest of the human turn. A fresh `InvasionGraph` could consequently choose a different next target than a cache rebuilt from the same post-raze state.

The repair makes removal report whether this cache actually contained the city, then re-sorts only those affected caches after destruction. It does not rebuild pathfinding, distances or asset scores beyond KI#547's separate owner aggregate. KI#550 is an inherited AdvCiv practical-2605 lifecycle/refactor regression retained in Base AdvCiv 1.14, not an AdvCiv-SAS regression. A full Huge Pangaea autoplay completed successfully after the repair; the exact post-destruction ordering remains source/lifecycle verified. Found as F227/provisional KI#550 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

<a id="ki-551"></a>

## KI#551 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI Permanent Alliance migration defect) Outsiders lost persistent history and obligations against the absorbed team

Permanent Alliance formation merges the absorbed leader's UWAI history into each member of the surviving team. The operation was only one-directional: no corresponding pass visited outside players whose persistent cache fields used the absorbed `TeamTypes` as a target key. Core team relations and wars migrate to the surviving identity, but outsiders permanently retained `m_aiPastWarScore`, sponsored-war bounty/sponsor pairs and `m_readyToCapitulateTo` under the dead team number. Ordinary cache refreshes deliberately preserve these event-maintained fields and have no producer capable of reconstructing their lost historical meaning.

For example, an outside AI hired to declare war on team B can remain physically at war when B joins surviving team A because `CvTeam::addTeam` transfers differing wars. Its paid obligation nevertheless remained stored against B; subsequent `HiredHand` evaluation queried current opponent A, found no sponsor or bounty, and could agree to peace earlier than the intended roughly 20-turn obligation. Past-war confidence against B was similarly orphaned. If an outside AI had already decided to capitulate to human B, absorption into a surviving human team A made `AI_surrenderTrade(A)` miss the readiness handshake and potentially return `DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL` solely because the target team identity changed.

The repair adds an explicit reverse-direction migration for every living outside major player. Before absorbed players join the surviving team, sponsored-war state adopts the absorbed sponsor when the survivor has none or the absorbed bounty is larger, matching the existing higher-bounty conflict policy; human-capitulation readiness is unioned onto the team that will be human after the merge. After player reassignment finalizes war-ending history, past-war scores are added to the surviving key. All four absorbed-team entries are cleared across these phases, while ordinary derived maps remain governed by their normal refresh cadence. Merged-team members are excluded, keeping this helper separate from the existing `UWAI::Team::addTeam` direction and avoiding the earlier live-iterator self-add defect.

The missing outsider direction dates to AdvCiv's initial 2017 WarAndPeace/UWAI Permanent Alliance support and remains in Base AdvCiv 1.14; later iterator and cache rewrites retained the same contract. KI#551 is therefore an inherited AdvCiv design omission rather than an AdvCiv-SAS regression. A rebuilt DLL completed a Huge Pangaea mixed-team autoplay with Permanent Alliances enabled through a turn-420 Space Race victory. `SASGameRecord_20260828T061105Z_new1.log` confirms the option and team setup; no new Permanent Alliance formed during the sample, so the exact outsider-state migration remains source/lifecycle verified rather than empirically triggered. Found as F228/provisional KI#551 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, and tested with the help of wonderingabout, thanks.

Update: KI#1045 found that this repair ran only after absorbed-player reassignment had already cleared sponsored-war and capitulation state. The migration is now split across the exact lifecycle boundary: transient obligations move before reassignment, while finalized past-war history moves after the absorbed team's zero-alive war teardown.

## KI#552 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv enum-map compression regression) Large sponsored-war payments could erase their own obligation

`UWAICache::reportSponsoredWar` converts the value received for declaring war into an integer utility and remembers it so the hired AI remains reluctant to end the war for roughly 20 turns. The source explicitly permits paying more than the AI demands to strengthen that reluctance. AdvCiv practical 3183 changed this formerly full-width integer storage to a signed-short `CivTeamMap<int,short>` during a nominally non-functional enum-map compression rewrite, but left the unrestricted integer producer unchanged. The normal release conversion is a narrowing cast. A sufficiently large legal positive payment could consequently wrap to a negative short, fail the function's immediate positive-value test and be normalized to zero with `NO_PLAYER` as sponsor: greater overpayment could erase the obligation entirely.

The repair computes the utility in full width and saturates it to `[0, MAX_SHORT]` before compact assignment. Values within range are unchanged; any larger supported payment now means the maximum remembered bounty instead of wrapping, preserving the intended monotonic relationship while retaining the current compact storage and save layout. The gold trade amount and deal value are ordinary integers, and human trade validation permits any specified amount covered by the treasury, so this is a reachable inherited AdvCiv practical-3183 regression rather than malformed input or an AdvCiv-SAS change. The exact high-payment diplomatic state remains source/arithmetic verified. Found as F229/provisional KI#552 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#554 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI cache defect) City-set changes left surviving target geometry stale

AdvCiv's incremental city-created/destroyed callbacks updated only the changed cached city. However, every foreign target's cached deployment distance, land reachability and capital-area flag derive from the cache owner's complete city set. Founding, acquiring or losing an own city could therefore leave all surviving foreign targets modeled from the old source cities. The aggregate reachable-city counts remained based on those stale target records as well. Capital loss was especially clear: the destruction callback ran before deletion and before `findNewCapital`, while target value also depends on capital status, yet no later refresh followed the replacement.

The repair introduces one targeted city-cache reconstruction that rebuilds uniquely indexed city wrappers, reachability counts, deployment geometry, target values, attack ordering and the owner's total asset score without disturbing unrelated persistent UWAI history. Creation invokes it only for the cache whose own city set changed; other observers retain the cheaper incremental update. Destruction still removes the old wrapper before its `CvCity` storage is freed, then a new post-mutation callback rebuilds the former owner's cache only after deletion and any capital replacement are complete. Capital replacement additionally rebuilds observer caches because their surviving target values can change; routine non-capital loss avoids that broader cost. This closes the unsafe timing gap without paying for a whole `UWAICache::update` on every city event.

Update: The repair-side audit found that the owner/capital-only optimization remained too narrow: ordinary foreign city creation or loss changes city-count and production-rank inputs used by every surviving target city's cached value. KI#1038 replaces incremental observer insertion and conditional post-destruction rebuilding with the same coherent city-derived reconstruction for every eligible observer. City events remain far less frequent than UWAI's ordinary per-turn work, while the cache can no longer expose mixed old/new target values between turns.

KI#554 is an inherited AdvCiv practical-2605 incremental-cache regression retained in Base AdvCiv 1.14, not an AdvCiv-SAS regression. A rebuilt Debug-opt DLL completed a Huge Pangaea Normal-speed autoplay through a turn-391 Domination victory. `SASGameRecord_20260901T075637Z_new1.log` records 116 city acquisitions, 166 `CITY_REMOVED` plot-change rows and nine eliminated players, providing substantial coverage of the repaired creation/destruction lifecycle; exact post-capital cache values remain source/lifecycle verified. Found as F231/provisional KI#554 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, and tested with the help of wonderingabout, thanks.

## KI#556 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI cache defect) Incremental human city creation omitted known-city handling

Full `updateCities` includes every city of a foreign civilization already known to a human cache owner, while an AI cache owner must still deduce the city site. AdvCiv practical 2606 added that human rule only to the full refresh; practical 2605's earlier incremental `reportCityCreated` retained the old same-team-or-deducible test. A newly founded city of a known foreign civilization could consequently remain absent from a human cache until its next full update, even though later AI military analysis deliberately uses that human cache when modeling the human's likely targets.

The incremental callback now mirrors both parts of the full-refresh membership contract: a foreign team must be met, then either the cache owner is human or the city site is deducible. Same-team cities remain eligible independently. The defect and split contract remain in Base AdvCiv 1.14, so KI#556 is an inherited AdvCiv regression rather than an AdvCiv-SAS change. The same Huge Pangaea autoplay completed successfully with the corrected membership logic and extensive city creation/acquisition activity; the exact known-but-not-deducible human-cache timing remains source/lifecycle verified. Found as F233/provisional KI#556 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, and tested with the help of wonderingabout, thanks.

## KI#557 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv UWAI lifetime defect) First-city callbacks could insert a duplicate cache entry

On ordinary first-city founding, `setFoundedFirstCity(true)` performs a full UWAI cache refresh after city initialization. The later normal `AI_cityCreated` broadcast then inserted a second separately allocated wrapper for the same plot. The vector accepted both wrappers while `std::map::insert` silently retained only the first. If that first city was captured after the founder obtained another city in the same round, destruction removed only the map-owned wrapper; the duplicate could retain a pointer to freed `CvCity` storage and be dereferenced by the next attack-priority sort. Saving and loading preserved the corrupt vector/map relationship rather than healing it.

The central add helper now establishes unique map ownership first, asserts duplicate keys in debug builds and safely discards an unexpected duplicate rather than exposing it through the vector. The ordinary creation callback explicitly replaces any existing observer wrapper with the final city snapshot, while creation by the cache owner uses KI#554's coherent city reconstruction. Destruction retains its pre-free removal and now receives KI#554's post-mutation reconstruction as a second safety boundary. This preserves the useful first-city early refresh instead of merely suppressing the later callback.

The regression arose from the composition of AdvCiv practical 1494's first-city refresh and practical 2605's generalized creation callback, and remains in Base AdvCiv 1.14. It was not introduced by AdvCiv-SAS. The same new-game autoplay exercised ordinary first-city initialization for all 16 starting players, extensive later city turnover and nine eliminations without a crash, then completed successfully. Found as F234/provisional KI#557 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, and tested with the help of wonderingabout, thanks.

<a id="ki-558"></a>

## KI#558 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv True Starts/UWAI lifecycle defect) Leader replacement left the former leader's military trait flags cached

AdvCiv initializes each major player's UWAI cache before `CvGame::setInitialItems` applies the supported True Starts option. True Starts can then replace that player's leader. `CvPlayer::changeLeader` correctly removes the former traits, installs the new leader and traits, and refreshes the ordinary AI personality without reinitializing UWAI, because wholesale reinitialization would destroy its persistent state. However, UWAI separately cached `m_bOffensiveTrait` and `m_bDefensiveTrait` only during initialization and serialization. Neither leader replacement nor ordinary cache updates recomputed them, so the former leader's military personality could persist for the entire game.

The cached flags affect distrust, invasion-force modifiers and Settler priority. Current SAS provides a direct defensive mismatch because Protective grants a city-defense promotion: changing between a Protective and non-Protective leader could retain phantom defensive modeling or omit the new leader's real modeling. Base AdvCiv can also stale its offensive flag because its Aggressive trait grants a generic-combat promotion.

`CvPlayer::changeLeader` now requests a targeted recomputation after the new traits and personality are installed. It does not reinitialize UWAI or disturb persistent war state. Old-save/XML reinterpretation hardening is deliberately omitted because AdvCiv-SAS supports only saves created by the current version. The defect arose when AdvCiv's correct earlier removal of blanket AI reinitialization was later combined with its True Starts integration, so KI#558 is an inherited AdvCiv integration defect rather than an AdvCiv-SAS regression.

A Huge Pangaea Normal-speed autoplay with True Starts completed successfully from turn 0 through its turn-500 Time victory, covering the supported True Starts startup sequence and continued UWAI operation. ## KI#560 - (Fixed inherited original UWAI/Base AdvCiv military-cache defect) Ordinary aircraft contributed zero actual Army power

UWAI's Army branch is explicitly documented to include air and siege units. Its typical-unit selection deliberately excludes aircraft because they should not represent a trainable land Army unit, but its incremental actual-unit inventory is a separate present-force census used by war utility and invasion simulations. That census admitted only units with positive ground `getCombat()` or nuclear capability. Fighters, Bombers, Stealth Bombers and Guided Missiles instead use positive `getAirCombat()` with zero ground combat; despite valid Army domains and positive XML power, they contributed neither units nor power to the cached actual Army.

The actual-unit admission gate now includes positive air combat alongside ground combat and nukes. Every branch still applies its own domain and positive `unitPower` filters, while typical-unit selection remains unchanged. The mismatch exists in the original UWAI military-branch design and Base AdvCiv 1.14, so KI#560 is inherited rather than introduced by AdvCiv-SAS. AdvCiv-SAS supports only saves created by the current version, so no migration for old serialized Army totals is added; new games and current-version save/reload use the corrected producer consistently.

A Huge Future Era Pangaea Normal-speed autoplay completed successfully from turn 400 through its turn-500 Time victory; its `SASGameRecord` recorded Guided Missile production, exercising the corrected ordinary-air census path. Found as F237/provisional KI#560 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 `UWAICache.cpp` audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#561 - (Fixed inherited original UWAI/Base AdvCiv military-population mismatch) Nuclear weapons distorted the conventional Home Guard split

Invasion simulation estimates the share of non-naval units committed to Home Guard, then applies that ratio to Army units and power. Nuclear power is deliberately removed from the power pool before this split, but the ratio's `m_iNonNavalUnits` denominator and Army unit count both included ICBMs and Tactical Nukes. Merely adding nuclear weapons could therefore lower the guard ratio and manufacture additional deployable conventional Army power even though the conventional force was unchanged. Excluding nukes only from the denominator would leave the same ratio incorrectly partitioning an Army headcount that still includes them.

Nuclear weapons are now excluded from the conventional non-naval denominator. InvasionGraph separately subtracts the Nuclear branch's unit count from Army before applying the guard ratio, then adds those nuclear units back unchanged; conventional Army power continues to be split before the existing limited nuclear contribution is added. Aircraft fixed by KI#560 remain conventional Army units and defensive aircraft remain eligible Home Guard units. This population mismatch exists in original UWAI and Base AdvCiv 1.14, so it was not introduced by AdvCiv-SAS.

The same Huge Future Era autoplay completed successfully, but produced no nuclear weapons; the exact nuclear partition therefore remains source/arithmetic verified rather than falsely claimed as directly exercised. Found as F238/provisional KI#561 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 `UWAICache.cpp` audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#562 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv/UWAI war-lifecycle defect) Elimination and early-scenario peace bypassed paid-war cleanup

Normal AdvCiv peace reports the war ending to both teams' UWAI caches before clearing war state. Each cache first forgets the sponsor and bounty of a paid declaration, then—when UWAI is ready—uses the still-live war success and reparations context to update its past-war history. Two inherited lifecycle paths bypassed that contract.

When a team's last member died, `CvTeam::changeAliveCount` ended every war through raw `setAtWar(false)` calls rather than `makePeace`, so surviving hirelings retained paid-war obligations against the eliminated team and omitted that war from their learned history. If the target was later revived and entered an unrelated war, `HiredHand` could reuse the ancient sponsor and bounty as though they paid for the new conflict. Separately, sponsored wars can be recorded during the first two turns of a scenario while UWAI is enabled but deliberately not ready; ordinary peace during that window skipped the whole war-ending report, including the transient cleanup that does not require ready evaluation caches.

Paid-war cleanup is now an explicit member-cache lifecycle operation separate from history evaluation. Ordinary early-scenario peace clears both teams' sponsorship while continuing to defer history. Elimination reports the ending war for each surviving enemy before raw teardown while the required war context remains intact; if that happens during the same readiness window, it performs only the safe cleanup. This fixes both the stale paid-war contract and the eliminated opponent's omitted past-war result without reusing full evaluation where its readiness assumptions do not hold. The bypasses exist in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and were not introduced by AdvCiv-SAS.

The same full autoplay eliminated eight teams between turns 184 and 439, repeatedly exercising the repaired elimination callback without an observed failure; no eliminated paid war was identified, so the exact stale-sponsorship sequence remains source-verified. Found as F239/provisional KI#562 during ChatGPT-5.6-Sol's C019 `UWAICache.cpp` audit; independently reviewed, fixed and documented with the help of GPT-5.6-Sol, thanks.

## KI#564 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv OneArea-resource clustering regression) Grouped copies bypassed placement caps and crossed landmasses

BtS and K-Mod place each `OneArea` resource type on selected landmasses and keep every grouped copy on the same landmass as its cluster center. They also stop adding copies once the map-wide target has been reached. AdvCiv practical 1268 extracted the duplicated group loop into `placeGroup`, whose default allowance is 100. The non-`OneArea` caller supplied its remaining target, but `addUniqueBonusType` accepted the default. Each cluster could consequently overshoot both `calculateNumBonusesToAdd`'s map-wide target and AdvCiv practical 129's first-pass per-area cap. The extracted AdvCiv clustering path also omitted the former same-area test, allowing a `OneArea` resource with a wider group range, currently Elephants with range 2, to cross a narrow water gap onto another landmass.

The repair passes `placeGroup` the remaining map-wide allowance, further limited by the remaining first-pass area allowance when that cap is active. The helper also enforces the resource's existing `OneArea` invariant in the normal AdvCiv clustering path; the optional BtS-style SAS branch already retained that boundary. Randomized plot order and AdvCiv's exponentially declining group probability are unchanged, as are all non-`OneArea` clusters. This regression remains in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and was not introduced by AdvCiv-SAS.

Current-build Huge Hub, Wheel, BTG Grid and Archipelago maps generated successfully. The BTG Grid game also saved and reloaded successfully, while the Archipelago map using its Tiny Islands option completed a turn-101 autoplay without an observed issue. ## KI#565 - (Fixed inherited AdvCiv OneArea-resource selection regression) Area ranking ignored map-script latitude policy

AdvCiv practical 2364 estimates each candidate landmass's suitability before choosing where to place a `OneArea` resource. The scan deliberately disables resource-range checks for speed, but it also hardcoded `bIgnoreLatitude` to false. Actual placement immediately afterward uses the map script's `isBonusIgnoreLatitude()` result. On scripts that request latitude-independent resources, including Wheel, Hub, Ring, BTG Grid and BTG Cross, valid polar plots were therefore excluded from area ranking and then accepted during placement. An area could be undervalued or rejected using a different eligibility contract from the operation the estimate was meant to predict.

The suitability scan now passes the same map-script latitude policy as actual placement while continuing to skip only the expensive range check. Standard scripts that do not ignore latitude are unchanged. The mismatch remains in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and was not introduced by AdvCiv-SAS. The same successful Huge Hub, Wheel and BTG Grid generation suite exercised scripts that ignore latitude; hidden area rankings remain source-verified.
